home_pitcher_note: A free-agent pickup brought in to provide some leadership, the 33-year-old gets his first big league Opening Day nod, partly because of injuries and largely because of performance.
away_pitcher_note: Santana, more than anyone else, has given the Mets reason to believe that they're better than last year. He's charged them with optimism and erased memories of last September -- and all that without throwing a pitch of any consequence.

home_pitcher_note: A 22-year-old from the Netherlands, VandenHurk got a taste of the big leagues last year when he was called up in early April because of an injury situation. He ended up making 17 starts and appearing in 18 games for Florida in his rookie season. The right-hander endured some predictable growing pains at the big league level. To get him more seasoning, he also pitched in '07 at Double-A and Triple-A. In all, he threw a career-high 147 1/3 innings a year ago.
away_pitcher_note: If Martinez was upset about losing his ace status to Johan Santana, he wasn't about to complain. Instead, he has said all the right things in regard to his new teammate, and now, he'll finally have a chance to back up those words on the mound. Set to start the season's second game against the Marlins, Martinez will also be embarking on what he hopes can be his first full season since 2005. Right rotator cuff surgery cut short the end of his 2006 season, after he missed nearly all of last summer recovering from the same operation. For his career, Martinez is 6-6 with a 2.85 ERA against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: One of the centerpieces in the trade with the Tigers for Dontrelle Willis and Miguel Cabrera, the 22-year-old Miller threw 64 innings with the Tigers a year ago. A first-round pick in the 2005 Draft, Miller may have the most overall talent in the rotation. The lefty, however, still is refining his skills, but he projects to be a frontline starter for years to come.
away_pitcher_note: Oliver Perez enters this season with a hefty contract -- and some hefty expectations. After winning his arbitration case in February and nearly tripling his salary to $6.5 million, Perez embarked on a spring that was quite typical of his career to date. Half the time, he was unhittable. The other half, he was anything but.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson surrendered two first-inning runs in Sunday's Opening Day start against the Nationals and then ended his outing by retiring 19 consecutive batters. He was 2-2 with a 3.33 ERA in four starts against the Mets last year.
away_pitcher_note: For much of last season, the Mets needed Maine to be their ace -- and he filled that role as best he could. This year, the Mets simply need him to be a rock -- and he's shown no reason why he can't fill that role even better.

home_pitcher_note: Smoltz will be making his season debut with a right shoulder that he says has proven to be healthy over the past week. The tightness he'd had between his neck and right shoulder wasn't present when he completed five innings in a Minor League game on Sunday. The veteran hurler's only Spring Training start against a big league team occurred on March 15 against the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Santana was in control throughout his Mets debut against the Marlins on Monday. If not for a two-run home run by Josh Willingham, he would have escaped unscathed. As it was, he allowed three hits and two walks and struck out eight in seven innings. But the Marlins' batting order and that of the Braves bear little resemblance. He threw 100 pitched and fatigue didn't appear to be an issue.

home_pitcher_note: Perez's '08 debut was a lopsided affair and not only because the Mets scored 13 runs behind him. He buried the Marlins, allowing five singles and a walk and striking out eight in six shutout innings. He'll have five days' rest when he pitches the Mets' opening home game, as Pedro Martinez's stand in, against a team that beat him twice in three games last season.
away_pitcher_note: The venerable lefty didn't have a very good start to his 22nd Major League season, and lasted only 3 2/3 innings. Five of the six runs scored off him came in the first inning, though he wasn't helped by two errors. He's gone 3-3 with a 2.59 ERA in eight starts at Shea Stadium, and 6-3 with a 2.87 ERA in 14 career starts against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey will have gone 11 days without pitching. Not recommended. He has opposed the Phillies once in his 18 big league starts, losing to them in Philadelphia July 1 last year. He allowed two earned runs in five innings. Jim Rollins hit a two-run against him.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick started 2008 in the same manner that allowed him to survive 2007. He put runners on base, then made the right pitch at the right time to keep the damage to a minimum. This has become a Kendrick standard. His outings won't look beautiful, and he won't strike out many, but he won't lose him composure, either, and that counts for a lot. He beat the Mets last season, allowing two runs in 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Maine needed 96 pitches to complete four innings in his 2008 debut and more offense from his teammates to avoid a loss. The Braves fouled off many pitches and didn't hit him all that hard. Maine has been quite successful against the Phillies -- 4-0 record and 2.13 ERA in six career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Eaton turned in a stellar 2008 debut on Saturday, allowing two runs in 7 2/3 innings. To put that in perspective, he lasted that long in a game once in his 30 starts last season. While one start can't erase the misery of his 10-10, 6.29 ERA year in 2007, Eaton and his teammates were encouraged by his economical outing. He is particularly good against the Mets, with a 5-0 record and a 2.68 ERA against them in seven career outings.

home_pitcher_note: Having pitched twice in relief last week and having not made a start in the big leagues since 2004, Figueroa has been chosen to replace disabled Pedro Martinez in the rotation -- for now. He has a 7-13 record and 5.17 ERA in 33 career starts in the big leagues. He is winless with two losses in his last four starts and hasn't won as a starter since he defeated the Brewers in August 2003.
away_pitcher_note: Parra recorded his first Major League victory after holding the Giants without a hit for five innings and finishing with two runs allowed in 5 1/3 frames. The lefty earned Milwaukee's fifth starter job out of Spring Training and looked more than capable in the first outing of 2008, hitting the radar gun as high as 97 mph in the first inning and effectively mixing his pitches. When Yovani Gallardo comes back in mid-April from a rehab assignment, the team will have a difficult decision facing it as to which starter?s spot Gallardo takes.

home_pitcher_note: Santana has pitched seven innings in each start and pitched well enough to win both. The Marlins and Braves have managed 12 base runners in 14 combined innings, and they have struck out 11 times. He has been, as advertised, yet he has split his first two decisions. He will be pitching with five-days rest. He has a 3-1 record and 3.32 ERA in against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets has not allowed a run in any of his first 15 1/3 innings, putting together back-to-back starts likely to rival any pair in his All-Star career. After 6 1/3 scoreless innings in rainy Wrigley Field on Opening Day, Sheets notched just the second shutout of his career -- and first since May 2001 -- with a dominant effort against San Francisco on Sunday. Sheets was on fire immediately, dismissing the first three batters on 11 pitches, and he needed just 109 to navigate the contest.

home_pitcher_note: Perez pitched in and out of trouble last Tuesday against the Phillies, walking three batters and hitting two. Still, his command was sharp enough to escape without any damage on the scoreboard, and he has yet to allow a run in 11 2/3 innings this season. Perez didn't face the Brewers last season, though he holds a 3-1 record and 4.32 ERA against them for his career.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan is Mr. April for Milwaukee and was on the verge of improving to 6-2 in the opening month since debuting with the team last season, only to see a win wiped away Tuesday. He worked six scoreless innings before a pair of seeing-eye singles led to a run in the seventh, and was in line for the win before Corey Patterson's two-out, two-strike home run off Eric Gagne in the ninth. Suppan has a 2.81 ERA in eight career starts against the Mets and a 2.70 ERA at Shea Stadium, numbers that don't include his eight scoreless innings in Game 6 of the 2006 NLCS for the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey wasn't efficient, needing 100 pitches to complete five innings during his season opener last Wednesday against the Phillies. But it was enough for a victory, and enough, he said, to help him with a certain confidence that he lacked last year. Pelfrey has faced the Nationals more than any other team, posting a 1-1 record and 5.64 ERA in four career starts.
away_pitcher_note: It looked like Perez was going to help the Nationals get out of their funk last week against the Marlins. Perez was staked to a 1-0 lead and cruising during the first five innings, allowing just two hits. But the Marlins started to get to him in the sixth. With one out, Hanley Ramirez scored the tying run on single by Jeremy Hermida. Two batters later, Mike Jacobs singled to put runners on first and second. Manny Acta took Perez out of the game, and it was time for the bullpen to work its magic. On this day, the relievers didn't get the job done and handed Perez the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Maine hardly was challenged in the first five innings in his most recent start, a no-decision victory against the Philliies Thursday. But he walked three batters, allowed a single and needed 24 pitches to extricate himself from the sixth inning without allowing a run. Then he surrendered a home run and a double to right-handed hitters before being removed. He struck out merely one of 26 batters, an abnormally low number for him.
away_pitcher_note: Chico made one mistake and it proved costly as the Nationals lost to the Braves, 1-0, at Nationals Park last Friday night. Chico pitched a great game, going eight innings and giving up one run on five hits. But his biggest mistake came in the sixth inning. Braves shortstop Yunel Escobar took the first pitch and hit the ball over the right-center field wall for his second home run of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Figueroa made an emotional start in front of his hometown crowd last Friday night, taking a no-hitter into the fifth inning and ultimately winning his first decision since 2003. He was efficient with his pitches, throwing first-pitch strikes with a fastball that rested around 87 miles per hour. The effort was enough to earn him a start against the Nationals, whom he's never faced. The last time Figueroa spent time in the Major Leagues, they were the Expos, and he produced a 2.81 ERA in four career starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan had nothing in the tank as he gave up six runs in four innings against the Braves last Saturday. Jeff Francouer did most of the damage, driving in five runs against the youngster. Lannan acknowledged that he didn't follow pitching coach Randy St. Claire's gameplan and he paid the price. After the game, Lannan spent almost an hour watching video with St. Claire.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels is coming off a win over the Cubs, in which he threw seven innings of scoreless one-hit ball. The lefty has been the Phillies' most reliable starter in the early weeks of 2008, turning in three quality starts in three outings. The 2007 All-Star didn't face the Mets during the Phillies' most recent trip to Shea Stadium, but he is 1-1 with a 2.77 ERA against them in four career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Santana lost his second straight decision last Saturday against the Brewers, serving up three home runs in his worst outing yet as a Met. Extending his pitch count to 113, Santana struck out seven and walked two, though the homers accounted for four of the five runs against him. He'll make his first appearance in this rivalry with the Phillies on Friday night, and will also make his career debut at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer is coming off a no-decision against the Cubs on Sunday in which he allowed four runs over five innings, striking out two and walking one. His lone win this season came against the Mets on April 8, when he held New York to two runs in six innings. A matchup to watch here will be Moyer against Mets first baseman Carlos Delgado. Delgado has hit eight home runs off the southpaw, second only to Manny Ramirez's 10.
away_pitcher_note: Though the Mets built an early lead for Perez on Sunday against the Brewers, he quickly lost it, serving up six runs in his second straight no-decision. Perez couldn't escape the fifth inning, allowing eight hits in total -- one of them a home run into Shea Stadium's second deck. The lefty struck out four and walked three. Perez pitched well in his first start against the Phillies, but a high pitch count limited him to only 5 2/3 innings of shutout ball.

home_pitcher_note: In the midst of a nice rebound from a miserable 2007, Eaton has allowed three runs in each of his three outings and pitched at least six innings. The Phillies have been so impressed with him that they juggled their rotation to allow for him to start on April 15, then be in line to toss against the division-rival Mets. The right-hander is 5-0 with a 2.90 ERA in his career against New York.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey pitched the strongest game of his career last Tuesday against the Nationals, completing seven innings for the first time since cracking the big leagues and holding a Major League opponent scoreless for the first time in his life. That's a tough act to follow, but he'll do his best against the Phillies, a team he's already seen once this year. Pelfrey beat them in his season debut, allowing two runs over five innings, and holds a 3.60 ERA against them in 10 career innings.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano matched a career high with three hits, including an RBI single, and picked up the win in his last start against the Reds. He gave up two runs on eight hits over seven innings. The switch-hitter helped himself by hitting singles from each side of the plate, and a double in the seventh. Zambrano is finally doing what the athletic trainers tell him to do as far as staying hydrated to avoid cramps. He's now fueled by bananas, drinks plenty of water, and avoids coffee.
away_pitcher_note: Though dissatisfied with his work, Maine pitched effectively enough against the Nationals on Wednesday night to gain his first victory -- five hits, four walks, four strikeouts in 6 2/3 innings. He senses the spring chill had affected his command and wouldn't be upset if summer paid an early, one-day visit to Wrigley Field on Monday. In three starts, he has yet to approach the level of effectiveness his final Spring Training appearances suggested.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly is still searching for the elusive first win. The lefty did post his longest outing of the season in his last start against the Reds on Thursday, but gave up five runs on six hits and three walks over the six innings. His velocity was better but he's still not right with his location. The three walks he issued snapped a streak of nine consecutive games issuing two or less dating to Sept. 5, 2007. This is the first time since 2002 that Lilly has begun the season 0-3.
away_pitcher_note: Figueroa is to make his third start in Pedro Martinez's stead. The Mets couldn't have expected much more from Martinez than Figueroa has provided. He pitched seven innings, allowing three hits, one a two-run home run by Nick Johnson, and two walks while striking out seven in his most recent start, against the Nationals on Thursday. He has pitched in three games at Wrigley Field, starting one. He has a 2.53 ERA over 10 2/3 innings at Wrigley.

home_pitcher_note: Redding earned the victory in his last game against the Marlins. He allowed just four baserunners over six innings -- three of them on hits -- but the Marlins' Josh Willingham touched him for a two-run home run. Overall, Redding is off to a nice start as one of the Nationals' most reliable pitchers.
away_pitcher_note: Santana was terrific in his last outing at Philadelphia, giving up four hits and three earned runs in seven-plus innings. He walked none and struck out 10, the 40th time in his career he has posted double-digit strikeouts. Santana threw 105 pitches, 70 for strikes and had excellent command of all of his pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Hill showed enough in his 2008 debut against the Marlins last Saturday to make the Nationals think he is picking up where he left off last season before he was injured. That means Hill, who fashioned a 3.42 ERA last year, could be pretty good. He had held the Marlins to a run before they hit him for three in the sixth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Perez threw a solid 5 2/3 innings on Saturday in his last start, holding the Phils scoreless in a 4-2 victory. Perez gave up four hits, but he surrendered a season-high five walks. It was the third time in Perez?s four starts this season he left a game without giving up a run. His seven strikeouts were his second most in a game this season, one behind his eight-strikeout performance on April 2 against Florida.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey had a shaky start in his last outing, giving up four runs and 10 hits over five innings against the Phillies on April 20 in a no-decision. Pelfrey has benefited from great run support in all three of his starts this season. The Mets produced eight runs in the Mets' 8-2 victory over Philadelphia on April 9 and six runs in a 6-0 win over Washington on April 15. He was down 4-0 against Philadelphia on Saturday, when the Mets responded with four runs in the sixth to get him off the hook with a no-decision. Pelfrey, however, did see his ERA balloon from 1.50 to 3.18.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens has continued to impress with an aggressive approach that proves he's not afraid to pitch to contact.  But with a lively fastball and a good changeup on Sunday afternoon, he recorded a career-high eight strikeouts and limited the Dodgers to one run in seven innings.  While his stuff is good, the Braves have been most impressed with the 22-year-old pitcher's composure and knowledge about pitching.

home_pitcher_note: Maine was inefficient on Monday, allowing the Cubs only two runs in six innings but needing 109 pitches to do it. Those runs were enough to give Maine his second loss, despite the fact that he shaved a sizable chunk off of his ERA for the third consecutive game. In Maine's previous start against the Braves, eight hits led to four runs in four innings. Maine defeated the Braves once last year in three tries.
away_pitcher_note: Concerns about Hudson's health were silenced on Monday night, when his fastball returned to its normal velocity -- between 91-93 mph.  On Wednesday in Florida, he lasted just three innings and couldn't throw his fastball above 85 (mph). Now that he's seemingly overcome the effects of the flu he fought two weeks ago, the veteran right-hander will look to claim his second win against the Mets.  He gained his first win of the year on April 5, when he allowed three earned runs in six innings against them.

home_pitcher_note: Figueroa held his own against a potent Cubs lineup on Tuesday, giving up three runs in five innings in an 8-1 loss at Wrigley Field. The Mets are happy with him in the rotation while Pedro Martinez rehabs his balky left hamstring, as Figueroa was something of a Spring Training revelation.
away_pitcher_note: John Smoltz became the 16th pitcher in Major League history to reach 3,000 strikeouts in his last start, a hard-luck loss to Washington on Tuesday. He has struck out 10 in back-to-back games for the first time since 1997. Smoltz, 40, has allowed just 15 hits and two runs in 23 innings, striking out 31 and walking six. His seven innings against Washington marked his longest outing of the season. He beat the Mets in his first start, allowing just two hits in five scoreless innings at Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Though Santana highlighted his last start with the two doubles he hit at the plate, his pitching certainly wasn't bad, either. Lasting seven innings in all against the Nationals, Santana allowed two runs on seven hits, striking out four and walking one. He can win his fourth game of '08 against the Pirates, a team he's only faced twice in his career. He started one of those game and added a relief appearance in the other, posting a combined 1.13 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: It took Snell nine hitters, four hits and four earned runs to warm up against the Cardinals in his last start on Wednesday, but the 26-year-old right-hander settled down and threw five scoreless innings to keep the Pirates in the game. Now, Snell will face a Mets team that has hit him hard throughout his career. In four appearances against New York, Snell has given up 12 earned runs in only 17 2/3 innings. He is 0-1 with a 6.11 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Perez started out strong last Thursday against the Nationals, breezing through four innings before walking the leadoff man in the fifth. He never recovered. The walk turned into a rally, and the rally turned into three runs. By the time Perez's night was complete, he had allowed five runs in all, walking four and taking his first loss. Perez, a former Pirate, holds a 5.14 career ERA against his old team.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny's seven walks his last time out set a career high for the left-hander and were the latest evidence of his season-long command woes. His usually steady changeup was consistently missing low in his more recent loss. The lefty has now walked 22 hitters in 22 1/3 innings, though Gorzelanny has said he feels he is on the verge of breaking through the rut. His chances of turning around his fortunes against the Mets aren't helped by his history against the New York club, however. In three career starts against the Mets, Gorzelanny is winless and has allowed 12 runs in 10 1/3 innings

home_pitcher_note: Owings may not make this start depending on how his sprained right ankle responds to treatment. If he is not able to go, Webb will start here and the team will plug Owings back in at some point. He hurt the ankle in his last start when he doubled and rolled the ankle when he stepped on the bag and had to leave the game. Owings wasn't at his best for the first time this year in that outing last Saturday against the Padres. The right-hander struggled with his command in the second inning as he hit a batter and walked three during a four-run San Diego rally.
away_pitcher_note: Maine threw 100 pitches in five innings against the Braves Saturday. One was wild, and allowed a run to score. He also allowed a run in the first before finding some sense of rhythm. He has yet to complete the seventh inning in his five starts, and, after a Spring Training which prompted teammates to anticipate a special season, he has yet to have a special outing.

home_pitcher_note: Webb just keeps rolling right along. In his last outing against the Padres on Sunday, he allowed one unearned run over six innings as he outdueled Jake Peavy for the 2-1 win. Hot starts are nothing new for Webb. The right-hander started the 2005 season 6-0 and opened the 2006 campaign with franchise-best 8-0 mark. Webb won the NL Cy Young Award in 2006 and finished second in the voting Peavy last year.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey's most recent start, Friday night against the Braves, was his least effective. He walked three of his first five batters and surrendered nine hits �- including a two-run home run by Kelly Johnson -- in 5 1/3 innings. He is winless in his two most recent starts, having allowed nine runs and 19 hits in 10 1/3 innings. He has taken two steps back since pitching seven shutout innings against the Nationals on April 15.

home_pitcher_note: The former A's right-hander has combined with Brandon Webb to create one of the top one-two punches in the National League. In his last outing, Monday night at home in a 5-3 victory over the Astros, Haren went 7 2/3 innings and was perfect for the first four before allowing two runs on three hits and two walks in the fifth. Manager Bob Melvin said afterward that Haren had his best stuff of his six Arizona outings. In that game he also had an RBI double, giving him two runs driven in this season. Haren was obtained from the A's on Dec. 14 in an eight-player deal that sent six prospects to Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: The only hits Santana allowed in his 5 2/3 innings against the Pirates on Tuesday in his most recent start were two home runs, the sixth and seventh he has surrendered in 40 1/3 innings. The first, by Nate McLouth, was the first allowed by Santana in the first inning in six starts this season. He surrendered 10 in first innings last season, when he led the American League in home runs allowed with 33.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley finally hit the win column with seven solid innings in Florida on Wednesday. For the fourth consecutive start, Billingsley struck out at least eight and the only run he allowed came on an infield single. He walked four, hit a batter and had two wild pitches, but pitched out of a pair of jams. He'll be starting against the Mets for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Perez's inability to deal with adversity, most of it of his own making, overwhelmed him again in his loss to the Pirates at Shea Stadium on Wednesday. He faced 16 batters, walked five, allowed two hits and hardly responded well to an error made behind him. He has walked 21 batters in 29 innings. The Mets have lost four of his six starts.
summary: 2008-05-05 - New York Mets (1) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda was efficient in a seven-inning no-decision against the Marlins on Thursday. He allowed only five hits, no walks and made 85 pitches, but he lost a lead by allowing a two-run homer to Cody Ross. After temporarily pitching out of the stretch in his previous rocky start, Kuroda seemed comfortable with his mechanics and returned to a conventional windup.
away_pitcher_note: The Mets skipped Figueroa's most recent turn in the rotation, after last Monday's game was rained out at Shea. He did, however, pitch 3 1/3 effective innings of relief two days later, holding the Pirates to one run on five hits. Figueroa threw 61 pitches in that outing and will return to the rotation on regular rest against the Dodgers, a team that he hasn't faced since 2002. This current group of Dodgers holds a .303 combined average against Figueroa, though none of the at-bats have come since 2004.
summary: 2008-05-06 - New York Mets (4) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Penny didn't have his velocity or command when he spotted the Rockies a three-run lead in wintry conditions at Coors Field, but he still picked up his ninth consecutive victory over Colorado. Although he went 2-1 against the Mets last year, he's 5-11 with a 5.66 ERA against them lifetime.
away_pitcher_note: Maine was inefficient in his latest outing, needing 107 pitches to complete six innings against the Diamondbacks, but wriggling out of two separate jams to allow only two runs in total. The effort was enough to net Maine his third win of the season, tying him with Jorge Sosa and Johan Santana for the club lead. Maine lost to the Dodgers twice in two starts last year, finishing with a 5.73 ERA.
summary: 2008-05-07 - New York Mets (12) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Santana allowed only one run in six innings in his last start against the Diamondbacks, but he needed 116 pitches to do it. That meant that the Mets had to turn to the bullpen early, and for his second straight outing, Santana saw a potential victory turn into a no-decision. Much of it was his own fault -- he walked four batters and allowed baserunners in every inning -- but his frustration was apparent. He'll look to rebound against the Reds, a team he hasn't faced in nearly seven years.
away_pitcher_note: Belisle's third start of the season was his best thus far. Over 5 1/3 innings on Saturday at Atlanta, he allowed two earned runs and eight hits without a walk and struck out two. He left trailing the Braves, 2-1, before the Reds took a 9-1 loss. Belisle did a better job of locating his pitches but he still wants to cut down on the high number of hits he's allowed. The right-hander had two starts and two no-decisions vs. the Mets with a 4.38 ERA (six earned runs over 12 1/3 innings) last season.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey was again inefficient last Saturday against the D-backs, allowing 13 total baserunners for the second straight game. Since winning his first two starts this season, Pelfrey has regressed, serving up 28 hits over the ensuing three outings. He's walked eight batters over his last two starts and struck out only two -- but perhaps there's relief in sight. In his only other start against the Reds -- the team he'll face on Saturday -- Pelfrey allowed two runs over six innings to record his second career win.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo is coming off the shortest outing of his career and a 14-7 loss to the Braves on Sunday. Lasting just 1 1/3 innings, all seven earned runs he allowed crossed in the second inning, when 11 men batted. The score was 7-0 when Arroyo left with one out in the second. Manager Dusty Baker voiced concerns after the game that something might be physically wrong with Arroyo. But Arroyo denied that he had any problems with his arm, saying he felt fine.

home_pitcher_note: Perez allowed at least five runs in an outing for the third straight start on Monday, boosting his ERA up to 8.10 over that span. Home runs, not walks, hurt him in that game, with the Dodgers tagging him for three homers and five runs in total. Perez beat Sunday's opponent, the Reds, twice with a 4.09 ERA in two starts last year, and he holds a 4.06 mark against them for his career. The lefty has yet to win at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto snapped a five-game winless streak and rebounded from a horrendous outing during a 5-3 win over the Cubs on Monday. The rookie right-hander threw six innings and allowed three earned runs and six hits with two walks and eight strikeouts. It was his first victory since April 3. Cueto benefited from personal instruction from mentor Mario Soto, who came up from the Dominican Republic to work with him after a string of rough outings. Cueto still threw a lot of pitches but limited his location mistakes.

home_pitcher_note: Figueroa lasted five innings against the Dodgers last Tuesday, tied for his shortest start of the season. It was enough to keep the Mets in the game but not enough to win it, with the offense unable to turn opportunities into runs. He'll instead search for his third victory against the Nationals, a team he held to two runs over seven innings last month. Figueroa struck out seven in that start, allowing only three hits.
away_pitcher_note: Odalis Perez can't seem to get a win. He pitched five innings Wednesday at Houston, giving up five hits and three runs despite being sick. He did not figure in the decision. He left with the Nationals down by one, but they quickly tied it on a Ryan Zimmerman homer. Perez struck out three and walked two, giving up a home run to Lance Berkman, the hottest hitter in the Houston lineup, and hitting a batter.

home_pitcher_note: Maine pitched longer than any Mets starter in nearly a year, lasting into the ninth inning in a 12-1 victory over the Dodgers on Wednesday. Sporting a fastball that reached 97 mph and a sharp changeup, Maine allowed four hits and one run. If not for a bloop double and a walk conspiring to end his day in the ninth, he might have recorded the second shutout of his career. Maine has beaten the Nationals once already this season, allowing two runs over 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan earned his third win in his last four starts when he beat Houston Thursday night, throwing six innings and allowing seven hits and just one run. He struck out three and walked only one. It was good enough to keep Washington from getting swept in a three-games series in Houston. He relied mostly on his changeup and slider against the Astros, throwing curveballs only to the last batter he faced in the game.

home_pitcher_note: The Mets purchased Vargas' contract from Triple-A New Orleans on Tuesday to make this start. The 29-year-old right-hander, 43-38 with a 4.95 ERA in parts of five seasons with the Expos, Nationals, D-backs and Brewers, went 1-1 with a 4.91 in two starts, walking one and striking out 11 in 11 innings, for New Orleans.
away_pitcher_note: One can say this much about Redding: When he has a bad outing, he is not afraid to say that he wasn't at his best. Last Friday was one of those days as the Nationals were pounded by the Marlins, 7-3, at Nationals Park. Redding lasted 5 1/3 innings and gave up six runs -- five earned -- on four hits. Manager Manny Acta said that Redding wasn't pounding the strike zone like he usually does. Redding walked five batters and three of them scored.

home_pitcher_note: Although he lost his third straight start Saturday, against the Reds, Pelfrey pitched more aggressively and impressively than he had since winning his first two starts. He all but abandoned his two-seam fastball, the one teammates call his "bowling ball" in favor of a rising fastball that produced more strikes, more swings and misses and more fly-ball outs.
away_pitcher_note: After Tuesday's game, Nationals manager Manny Acta announced that Bergmann will make the start against the Mets on Thursday. It will be Bergmann's second stint with the club this season. He made the Opening Day roster, but was soon shipped to Columbus on April 12. After posting the best ERA in Spring Training, Bergmann had a tough time getting people out once the season began, giving up 16 runs over 12 1/3 innings. Bergmann's worst game came on April 9 against the Marlins. He was cruising the first four innings, but in the fifth inning, the Marlins scored seven runs. A few days later, it was more of the same as Bergmann gave up four runs against the Braves.

summary: 2008-05-16 - New York Mets @ New York Yankees (Postponed)

home_pitcher_note: Pettitte only lasted four innings in his last start, taking a rare defeat at Tropicana Field after he ran into trouble in a lengthy fourth inning. Escaping one bad inning has been a recent problem for Pettitte, who has lost his last three decisions after starting the year 3-1. Pettitte has made 16 starts against the Mets dating to 1997, going 7-3 with a 3.42 ERA. He faced the Mets last May 18 at Shea Stadium, taking the loss after allowing three runs on five hits over seven innings in a 3-2 decision.
away_pitcher_note: Santana allowed 10 hits -- that equaled his career high -- walked one and struck out five in six innings in his most recent start Saturday against the Reds. Despite allergies that bothered him, he threw 116 pitches. His stuff wasn't sharp, but the Mets won for the sixth time in his eight starts, including his five most recent outings.
summary: 2008-05-17 - New York Mets (7) @ New York Yankees (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Wang narrowly avoided a tough-luck loss in his last start, which morphed into a tough-luck no-decision only because Hideki Matsui hit a ninth-inning homer to tie Tuesday's game at Tampa Bay. Wang worked seven innings against the Rays, allowing a run on seven hits while walking three -- tying a season high -- and striking out two. He wasn't especially pleased, but said it was "OK." Wang has faced the Mets once before in his career, on June 17 of last season at Yankee Stadium, when he came one out shy of a complete game in the Yankees' 8-2 victory. Wang allowed two runs on six hits that night, walking one and striking out 10 to outduel Orlando Hernandez.
away_pitcher_note: Perez shut out the Reds, who had 29 hits in the doubleheader the previous day, on one hit, three walks, a hit batsman for five innings, striking out eight Sunday afternoon. But a six-batter sequence in the sixth produced three runs and ended his workday at 102 pitches. He has a 3-1 record and 3.04 ERA in four career starts and 26 2/3 innings against the Yankees. Hideki Matsui has hit two home runs in seven career at-bats against Perez.
summary: 2008-05-18 - New York Mets (11) @ New York Yankees (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Glavine will be making his first start against the Mets since signing a one-year, $8 million deal with the Braves in November. Glavine recorded his first win of the season Wednesday against the Phillies, allowing four runs on four hits in 5 2/3 innings that gave the Braves a rare road win. It was his first win since September 8, 2007 and his first win in a Braves uniform since Sept. 19, 2002. He has pitched well this season, allowing two runs or less in five of his seven starts. The 304-game winner spent 16 seasons with the Braves before pitching the last five with the Mets, when he compiled a record of 61-56 with a 3.98 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Maine won his fourth straight start, throwing 109 pitches in six innings against the Nationals Tuesday. One of the two runs charged to him was unearned. He surrendered a home Zimmerman, the fourth he has allowed what now is 48 innings. Maine allowed one other hit, hit one batter and walked one. He struck out five.He has allowed no more than two runs in seven straight starts, the longest streak of that nature by a Mets starter since Masato Yoshii had eight such starts at the end of his 1999 season.

home_pitcher_note: Campillo will make his second Major League start during the second game of Tuesday's doubleheader against the Mets. Campillo hasn't made a start since 2005 when he was with the Mariners. In that start, he lasted just one inning before taking himself out of the game with a right elbow injury. Turns out that injury would require Tommy John elbow ligament transplant surgery three weeks later. Campillo has allowed three earned runs in 21 1/3 innings of relief this season. He has been used primarily as a long relief specialist, as he has pitched two or more innings in seven of his 13 appearances this season.
away_pitcher_note: Vargas allowed two runs over 6 1/3 innings of his Mets debut, leaving a tie game but taking the loss when Aaron Heilman allowed his inherited run to score. He struck out six Nationals and walked four. Vargas, whom the Mets signed to a Minor League contract last month, faced the Braves only in a relief capacity last year, when he was a member of the Brewers. He allowed four runs over 1 2/3 innings in that outing, though he holds a 4-1 record and 3.94 career ERA at Turner Field

home_pitcher_note: Pitching on short rest for the first time in his young career, Jair Jurrjens allowed two runs -- none earned -- on eight hits in a 3-2 win on Friday over the A's. In five innings, the 22-year-old surrendered three walks and struck out three, but had no-decision. The A's eight hits were the most allowed by Jurrjens since his April 8 start against the Rockies (nine hits). Still, Jurrjens has not given up more than four runs in any of his nine outings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey pitched six innings of no-hit ball against the Nationals last week, eventually allowing three hits -- and one run -- but nothing else. That was enough for him to take the loss, as his own offense could muster anything off of Jason Bergmann. Since discarding his mouthpiece and deciding to throw fewer sinkers, Pelfrey has been brilliant, losing twice but making noticeable strides in his game. He'll look to continue that trend against the Braves, a team that tagged him for five runs in 5 1/3 innings in April.

home_pitcher_note: After looking spectacular in three straight starts, Tim Hudson uncharacteristically struggled with his control on Saturday against the A's. The Braves ace gave up season highs in runs (five), home runs (two) and walks (five) in five innings. Entering Saturday's start, Hudson ranked third in the National League with fewest walks per nine innings (1.6). Hudson didn't pitch into the sixth inning for just the third time in 10 starts this season. He allowed two homers Saturday, which doubled his previous season total. The loss to the A's also snapped a personal three-game win streak.
away_pitcher_note: The home runs that have vexed Santana throughout his Mets career were again present Sunday against the Yankees, when he allowed three of them but managed to win anyway. Pitching into the eighth inning, Santana allowed four runs in all, giving up seven hits, walking two and striking out five. Following the game, he ranked fourth in the Majors with 11 home runs allowed, but also sixth in the National League with five wins. Santana lost to the Braves in his first outing against them this season, despite giving up only one run in seven innings at Turner Field.

home_pitcher_note: Reynolds is off to a good start in his first two big league appearances, showing poise on the mound and promising stuff. He has shown the confidence to throw a hard breaking curve and a changeup in secondary counts, and is commanding a good sinking fastball. The 6'7", 21-year-old was born with a downhill plane, a handy characteristic for a pitcher, particularly in Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Perez earned his second straight victory, pitching into the eighth inning for the first time in nine starts this season, while beating the Yankees on Sunday. He allowed three hits and two walks, struck out four in  7 2/3 innings and won for the second time in five starts. He has a 2-3 record and 7.24 ERA in six career appearances and 32 1/3 innings at Coors Field. His career record against the Rockies is 5-5.

home_pitcher_note: Francis, the Rockies' Opening Day starter, finally earned his first win in his ninth trip to the hill Sunday, holding the Twins to two runs on six hits and two walks (one intentional) in 6 1/3 innings.  His command was much improved, and he was especially effective with his offspeed stuff, most notably his changeup, which he was able to give some sink at times, and other times have it cut away from left-handers.  He gave up leadoff extra-base hits in four of the seven innings he was on the mound and a one-out triple in another inning, stranding all but one of those runners.  He only had one multihit inning, with the Twins only runs coming on a leadoff double and a full-count, two-run homer from Justin Morneau.
away_pitcher_note: Mets manager Willie Randolph pulled Claudio Vargas after just 66 pitches on Tuesday in hopes that he could bring the right-hander back on three days' rest to start against the Rockies. Vargas allowed four runs on five hits in five innings against the Braves, taking the loss, his second in as many starts this season. Vargas also lost May 14 against the Nationals, when he was charged with three hits, two runs and four walks in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cook has lost two straight starts after winning a club-record six straight. He grasped for control during the first four innings of his last start, against the Giants, giving up four runs in the first four innings. But after a brief pointer from pitching coach Bob Apodaca to stay compact in his delivery, he pitched three strong innings to last through the seventh. He's trying to take that feeling into his next start.
away_pitcher_note: It now appears the standard M.O. for Maine's opponents is to foul off pitches by the dozens in an effort to tire the Mets starter. Maine has thrown 325 pitches in his three most recent starts, covering 18 1/3 innings. His loss to the Braves on Tuesday was his first after four consecutive victories. He needed 99 pitches to achieve 12 outs.

home_pitcher_note: After two effective starts, one in which he made folks think a no-hitter was possible, Pelfrey endured a poor outing against the Braves Wednesday night. He faced 24 batters in four innings, 12 of them reached base and six of them -- a season high for him -- scored. Pelfrey now has lost five straight decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco's last start is probably one he'll remember for a long time to come. Against the Diamondbacks on Wednesday, Nolasco found himself matched up against the hottest pitcher in baseball at that point, Brandon Webb. Webb was 9-0 in nine starts coming into the game, but Nolasco pitched seven innings of one-run ball to give Webb his only blemish of the season. The 6-foot-2 righty allowed just three hits and struck out seven. It was Nolasco's longest outing since Aug. 13, 2006, at Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: The Braves swung at pitches early in the count when they beat Santana in Atlanta Thursday. That kept his pitch count down -- 90 in seven innings -- but Santana allowed a career-high 12 hits in those six innings. His winning streak ended at four games. The Mets had won his previous six starts.
away_pitcher_note: One day after turning 23, Miller turned in the start of his life. En route to the Marlins' fourth sweep of the season, the 6-foot-6 lefty turned in seven full innings of shutout ball while striking out a career-high nine hitters. Miller allowed just one runner to get in scoring position and dropped his ERA .85 points to help the Marlins sweep the Diamondbacks, who came into the series with the National League's best record.

home_pitcher_note: Perez struggled through five innings and two batters Friday night at Coors Field, walking a career-high eight and yielding four runs while giving up six hits, including a two-run homer. He has allowed five home runs in his last four games. Though he kept the Mets in the game and left with the score tied, earning a no-decision in the 13-inning defeat, he is in a rut on the road, going 1-2 with a 5.92 ERA in his last four starts away from Queens. He has not fared much better at home, going 1-1 with a 5.60 ERA at Shea this season.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off his worst outing of the season, Olsen was lifted after 3 1/3 innings and 81 pitches in a loss to the Giants last Friday. The left-hander hadn't gone shorter than five innings in his previous nine starts. Olsen was tagged for two home runs, but his fastball velocity reached 89 on a couple of occasions. That's the hardest he's thrown in a few outings. Lifetime against the Mets, he is 1-2 with a 3.94 ERA in eight games.

home_pitcher_note: Vargas came up big for the Mets at Coors Field Saturday, earning his first win in three starts since his May 13th callup. Pitching on three-day's rest a day after the Mets 'pen was extended in a 13-inning loss to the Rockies, Vargas went seven strong innings, holding Colorado to two runs on four hits. He struck out three and walked only one, inducing eight ground-ball outs with a sinker that played well in the offensively oriented ballpark. He improved to 5-1 against the Rockies, and will try to remain undefeated against the Dodgers, who he has faced once, a complete game victory in 2005 when he allowed one run on six hits while striking out seven.
away_pitcher_note: Penny showed improvement after three really rocky starts, but he still didn't get a win his last time out. This time it was one bad inning, which included back-to-back walks. Penny has had some shoulder stiffness to deal with, but he said after his last start he felt better than he had in five years. His velocity topped at 97 mph, which eased concerns about anything serious physically. But he's still allowing too many hits.
summary: 2008-05-29 - Los Angeles Dodgers (4) @ New York Mets (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Maine had a strong outing at Coors Field on Sunday, holding the Rockies to three hits and four walks over six innings while striking out a season-high eight, but it wasn't enough to match the complete-game one-run outing by Aaron Cook. Maine allowed four runs (three earned), and through the first five innings the only hit the Rockies had touched him for was a three-run homer that followed an error on a potential double-play grounder that would have ended the inning. His changeup was off, but he had good velocity. The Rockies were patient in laying off his pitches out of the zone, forcing him to throw strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw was impressive in his Major League debut on Sunday, limiting St. Louis to two runs on five hits over six innings. The only thing that kept him from getting his first career win was Albert Pujols, who drove in the first Cardinals run and set up the second, and the Dodgers bullpen that surrendered the lead. Overall, Kershaw threw 102 pitchers, 69 for strikes, and consistently touched 96 mph on the radar gun. He struck out seven, including three in the first inning.
summary: 2008-05-30 - Los Angeles Dodgers (9) @ New York Mets (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The 6-foot-7 righty has fallen into a steep slump of late, as he lost his sixth consecutive decision on Monday by giving up four earned runs in four innings to the Marlins. In that short outing, Pelfrey still threw 95 pitches in the 7-3 Mets loss, 52 of those tosses for strikes. And Pelfrey's ERA has suffered in the process, rising from 1.50 on April 15 to his current 5.33 mark.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley allowed his first home run in a month but continued to pitch like an ace against the Cubs. Working with an extra day of rest, he went six innings and struck out seven, but was lifted for a pinch-hitter with the Dodgers trailing by a run after making only 83 pitches. Billingsley has quality starts in five of his past six appearances.
summary: 2008-05-31 - Los Angeles Dodgers (2) @ New York Mets (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Mets manager Willie Randolph believes Santana will only get better as the year goes on and the weather gets warmer, but he showed on May 27 against the Marlins that he can be the true stopper New York is looking for right now. He pitched seven innings and struck out seven in a 5-3 win over Florida, improving his record in games following a loss to 33-24 since the 2004 season. In those games, Santana has allowed three runs or less 54 times.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda continued to be the tough-luck starter on the staff with another wasted effort in Chicago. After throwing six scoreless innings in the cold, he saw a win turn into a loss in the seventh when his defense and bullpen betrayed him. Kuroda allowed only one earned run in 6 1/3 innings and has allowed more than three earned runs only once in 11 starts.
summary: 2008-06-01 - Los Angeles Dodgers (1) @ New York Mets (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez ended a streak of five consecutive winless starts last Wednesday in an 11-3 triumph at Arizona. He blanked the Diamondbacks for five innings, then left the game after surrendering two runs in the sixth. Sanchez has been relying on a sinking fastball to neutralize hitters. It's a pitch he said he was told to abandon as a Minor Leaguer in 2004, but he resumed using it earlier this season.
away_pitcher_note: For his fourth straight start, Perez's pitch count hit the century mark on Wednesday. Three of those tosses were big mistakes -- two homers by Marlins outfielder Cody Ross and another by catcher Mike Rabelo. Perez didn't relinquish much, though, until in his sixth and final inning, as he surrendered three runs to force his second consecutive no decision. That's 210 pitches in two no-decisions.
summary: 2008-06-02 - New York Mets (2) @ San Francisco Giants (10) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Zito pitched respectably in his last outing but received a no-decision in a 4-3 victory at Arizona. Justin Upton, mired in a 1-for-29 skid, homered and lashed an RBI triple to nag Zito, who lasted six innings and allowed three runs for his fifth quality start in 11 outings. Zito excelled last year against the Mets, who reportedly were interested in him when he became a free agent following the 2006 season. He won both of his starts against New York, recording a 2.08 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: He strained his left hamstring after 3 1/3 innings of his season debut, but now, after nearly two months of rehab, Martinez is ready to return. Because the injury affected only his leg, Martinez was able to keep his right arm in relatively good shape while rehabbing in Port St. Lucie, Fla. So when he takes the mound against the Giants, he shouldn't have any problems with his velocity or endurance. The Giants were a different team when Martinez last faced them back in 2004. That also marked his only career appearance at AT&T Park, and he allowed four runs in six innings.
summary: 2008-06-03 - New York Mets (9) @ San Francisco Giants (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Cain struggled in the third frame of his previous outing, allowing three runs against the Padres, but ended up lasting through the seventh without surrendering another score. Not bad, considering he was hit on the right forearm in the first inning by a Brian Giles line drive. Alas, he had nothing to show for his effort, leaving with six strikeouts but no decision. It was the third time in 2008, and the sixth time since 2006, that Cain faced Greg Maddux, against whom he has an 0-3 record. The right-hander has allowed three runs or less in six of his last eight outings.
away_pitcher_note: Maine struggled early against the Dodgers on Friday night at Shea Stadium. After opening the game with four straight balls to put Juan Pierre on base, he gave up three hits and three runs in the first inning to give L.A. the quick advantage. But Maine bounced back, surrendering just two hits and one run through the next five innings to come away with a no-decision. In 101 pitches, he recorded six strikeouts and one walk. Maine impressed manager Willie Randolph with his ability to settle down and find his rhythm.
summary: 2008-06-04 - New York Mets (5) @ San Francisco Giants (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Six days after he tossed six scoreless innings in the Padres' 18-inning victory over Cincinnati, Banks took a four-hit shutout into the ninth inning before allowing a two-out, RBI single to Giants center fielder Aaron Rowand. It was Banks first complete-game victory and it came in just his second Major League start. Banks, who had five strikeouts and didn't walk a batter, threw 60 pitches through six innings 70 through seven and 83 pitches through eight innings. He finished with 101 pitches, 69 of them strikes. Banks has allowed one unearned run in his first three games with the Padres, spanning 17 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Mets must make a roster move before Pedro Martinez starts Tuesday night, and that move probably won't involve Mike Pelfrey. The club intends to retain Pelfrey in the rotation -- that wasn't necessarily the plan until he pitches effectively Saturday -- shift Claudio Vargas to long relief and demote Carlos Muniz. An injury to a pitcher could change all that. Pelfrey allowed seven hits, a walk and two runbs in seven innings against the Dodgers Sunday, his second encouraging in four.
summary: 2008-06-05 - New York Mets (1) @ San Diego Padres (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Wolf looked good in his last start on June 1 against the Giants at AT&T Park, allowing just four hits over six innings. Unfortunately for him, one of the hits he allowed was a sixth-inning solo home run to Aaron Rowand. Wolf had command of his fastball and breaking ball against the Giants, finishing with five strikeouts and one walk. He was 9-4 with a 3.44 ERA in 25 career starts against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Santana reeled in his 100th win on Sunday, and he did it in dominating fashion, pitching 7 2/3 innings and allowing one run to go along with six strikeouts. Even after relinquishing the lead in the first inning, Santana remained aggressive with his fastball and closed out multiple batters with his off-speed pitches. Of course, he is still adjusting to National League lineups, which also means he hasn't seen much of the Padres. In two career appearances vs. San Diego, Santana is 1-1 with a 3.55 ERA.
summary: 2008-06-06 - New York Mets (1) @ San Diego Padres (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The Padres staked Baek to a 3-0 lead after the first inning in his debut as a starter for San Diego on June 2, but the right-hander couldn't make it stand as the Cubs -- the highest-scoring team in the Major Leagues -- essentially peppered him for nine hits in 4 1/3 innings. Baek allowed four runs and three extra-base hits. He's scheduled to start against the Mets on June 7, though the team could always look at other options though with Jake Peavy and Chris Young on the disabled list, there aren't many.
away_pitcher_note: Perez reached what the Mets only can hope is the nadir of his uneven season in a cameo appearance against the Giants Monday night. The team's most erratic starter allowed six runs and retired one batter. He surrendered two home runs, three other hits and three walks. The home runs were the 10th and 11th against Perez in 60 innings this year. They also were the 14th and 15th he has allowed in the first inning since the beginning of last season, the most in the Majors. Perez has a 9.53 ERA in the first inning this season. The Mets have lost seven of his 12 starts.
summary: 2008-06-07 - New York Mets (1) @ San Diego Padres (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Ledezma was done in by his command more than anything else in his last start against the Cubs on Tuesday. The left-handed Ledezma allowed three runs on three hits over 4 2/3 innings but walked five, one intentionally. He also walked a run in with the bases loaded for already the second time this season. Ledezma retired eight of the first nine batters that he faced but battled his control thereafter. He threw 100 pitches, but 44 of them were balls.
away_pitcher_note: With his tongue in his cheek, Willie Randolph said what he wanted to see from Martinez was merely a quality start. That much was provided along with some promise when Martinez pitched well -- not exceptionally -- against the Giants Tuesday in his first start since April 1. He allowed three runs on seven hits and three walks. He struck out three -- two coming on a nasty changeup and nastier curve. And he showed he had some stamina, throwing 109 pitches.
summary: 2008-06-08 - New York Mets (6) @ San Diego Padres (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Maine defeated the Giants rather methodically on Wednesday in San Francisco, winning for the first in four starts. He could have been more effective, but he was effective enough, walking one and allowing seven hits and two runs, one unearned, the other slightly tainted, in six innings. He has a 2-1 record and 2.50 ERA in three career starts against the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Owings was roughed up by the Brewers on Wednesday afternoon at Miller Park. The right-hander left too many pitches up and out over the middle of the plate and paid for it by allowing five runs (four earned) on eight hits over just three innings. Owings has now lost three of his last four decisions. In his start prior to his last one, he didn't have his best against the Nationals and battled through 6 1/3 innings. The big blow came when Willie Harris touched him for a three-run homer with one out in the seventh. That broke open a 3-3 game and sent the Nats on the way to the win.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey provided another flawed but, in a perverse way, impressive start Thursday night against the Padres. He allowed 11 base runners in six innings, but held the Padres' less-than-fearsome offense to one run. He had pitched effectively three times in his five most recent starts -- a 1.74 ERA in 20 2/3 innings -- but has one loss and two no decisions in the three games. Call it growing pain, but he does seem to be making progress.
away_pitcher_note: Webb became the Major Leagues' first 11-game winner with his second successive effective start, holding Pittsburgh to one run and three hits over seven innings and driving in a run during the Arizona Diamondbacks' 3-1 victory on June 6. The right-hander has permitted only one extra-base hit -- Jason Bay's RBI double while giving up nine hits and one run in 16 innings over his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Santana doesn't expect the bruised left shoulder he suffered Friday in San Diego to interfere with his next assignment. The off-day Monday benefits him in that regard. He allowed one earned run in six innings (100 pitches). The one unearned run was the result of his throwing error. Since he lost his first Shea Stadium start, he has a 3-0 record -- and the team record is 4-0 -- in four starts. He pitched to no decision against the D-backs in Phoenix May 4, allowing one run in six innings in a Mets victory.
away_pitcher_note: Haren received a no-decision in his last start at Pittsburgh on Saturday. He pitched seven innings and allowed three runs and five hits. The right-hander struck out six and walked one. He admitted that he didn't have his best stuff, but he battled for seven innings in a game the D-backs won, 4-3.

home_pitcher_note: Perez recovered from his woeful start against the Giants on Monday and threw well enough against the Padres on Saturday. He allowed one run -- on a home run -- in 5 1/3 innings, surrendering four hits and two walks and hitting two of his last three batters. Now he is to face the Rangers and their dangerous batting order. It could be ugly or he could bury them. But it's always that way with Perez.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman gave the Rangers a strong start his last time out, holding the Rays to two runs on five hits and two walks in seven innings while striking out five. summary: 2008-06-17 - New York Mets (1) @ Los Angeles Angels (6) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: Maine did what he always seems to do, pitching a solid six innings on Wednesday while only allowing two runs on five hits. away_pitcher_note: Armas will probably get the call up from Triple-A for a fill-in start on Tuesday, and, depending on how he pitches, the 30-year-old veteran could potentially assume the long-relief role for the Mets in place of fellow callup Carlos Muniz. summary: 2008-07-01 - New York Mets (7) @ St. Louis Cardinals (4) (Final)

summary: 2008-07-02 - New York Mets (7) @ St. Louis Cardinals (8) (Final)

Eaton has yet to factor in a decision in two starts against the Mets this season. He has allowed seven runs on 11 hits in 11 innings against them.
away_pitcher_note: The first six batters Martinez faced last Wednesday in St. Louis hit the ball hard, and four of them wound up scoring. Martinez never recovered. His ERA over that three-game stretch is 10.20, and he'll be hard-pressed to find improvement against the Phillies, one of the most potent offensive teams in the league. Martinez did find success against them last September, striking out nine Phillies and allowing one run over six innings. But he took a no-decision in an eventual Mets defeat.

home_pitcher_note: The beneficiary of more impressive run support -- the Mets have scored a combined 24 runs over his last two starts -- Pelfrey won his fourth straight decision last Thursday in St. Louis. away_pitcher_note: Lincecum avoided the Sports Illustrated cover jinx in his last start, although he wasn't at his best. summary: 2008-07-08 - San Francisco Giants (0) @ New York Mets (7) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: After a string of three consecutive quality starts, Sanchez hit a snag in his last outing, against the Dodgers. In his only start against the Mets this season on May 11, Cueto was roughed up for six runs on eight hits through just 4 2/3 innings in a losing effort.
away_pitcher_note: Santana's start was shortened by another rain delay, but he finally got a win after throwing five shutout innings on Wednesday against the Giants.
