In his only start against the Mets this season, Arroyo pitched eight strong innings, giving up just one run on four hits with two walks and nine strikeouts. He reached his highest pitch count of the season -- 115 -- in that start. The eight innings were also his longest of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Maine's left forearm didn't cramp up as it did in Philadelphia, but his stat line from Thursday' start against the Giants was most definitely cramped: 4 2/3 innings, two hits, three earned runs, five walks, two wild pitches and eight strikeouts. All together, it was a lot of everything for a short outing turned no-decision, including a workload of 109 pitches (63 of which were strikes). In his last three starts, Maine has averaged slightly more than 4 2/3 innings and has not escaped the sixth inning. He hasn't fared much better against the Reds, either, sporting a 10 ERA with a 0-2 record in nine career innings.

home_pitcher_note: Fogg's return to the Reds' rotation has been solid. In two starts since coming off the disabled list, he's given up a total of just four earned runs and seven hits, though he received a no-decision in each. Fogg pitched 5 1/3 innings and gave up just three runs on one hit in his last start at Milwaukee on July 11. He struck out six and walked two.
away_pitcher_note: Though Perez regressed in one sense on June 11 against the Rockies, walking six batters, he also featured what both manager Jerry Manuel and catcher Brian Schneider called his best fastball of the season. That was enough to hold the Rockies to only one run over six innings, and keep this run of consistency going. It's now been three straight quality starts for Perez, who has produced a 0.90 ERA over that stretch. Perez, a veteran of the NL Central, has seen the Reds more than any other team in his career, and has compiled a 9-3 record and 4.09 ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez will be throwing on regular rest after pitching in the seventh inning of the All-Star Game on Tuesday. He gave up a game-tying two-run home run to J.D. Drew but had two strikeouts. In his last start, Volquez pitched seven solid innings, giving up just two runs on six hits with two walks and 10 strikeouts. He's won two straight and has just one loss in his past nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey continued his abrupt about-face the day before the All-Star break against the Rockies, gaining his sixth victory in six starts. Pelfrey has started four of the team's six shutouts. He pitched eight innings Sunday, extending his scoreless innings streak -- it spans three starts -- to 16. He has allowed one run in his three most recent starts (22 innings). He allowed six hits, and for the second straight start -- and the second time in his career -- he walked none. He hit a batter and struck out five. His start was moved up two days because Pedro Martinez's start had to be postponed two days.

home_pitcher_note: Santana, often hurt by home runs, surrendered consecutive home runs along with a single, double, and triple in one grotesque inning, the fourth, against the Reds Thursday. He allowed five runs, equaling the most he allowed in any start this season, but for the first time, all five runs were earned. He threw 92 pitches on a warm night. With an off-day Monday, he should be fully rested for the Phillies. He has allowed five runs and no walks and struck out 16 in 15 innings in two starts -- a victory and a no-decision -- against the Phillies this year.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton will have some extended rest when he makes his debut with the Phillies on Tuesday. The 27-year-old hasn't pitched since July 9, when he got shelled for six runs off nine hits in six innings against the Mariners. Blanton was scheduled to start on Friday with the Athletics, but after the trade, the Phillies moved him back to his next scheduled outing. The fifth-year pitcher will be debuting against a Mets team he has had great success against in the past. In two previous starts against New York, Blanton has thrown 15 shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: With his loss to the Reds on Friday, Maine has gone four starts without a victory -- he had lost twice -- and he has pitched merely 19 innings in the process. He has been neither effective nor particularly lucky. Maine's two starts against the Phillies this season have produced modest performances and no decisions, but each was a part of a Mets victory. His career numbers against them before this season include a 4-0 record and 2.13 ERA. And he's been more successful at Shea than he has been elsewhere -- 4-1 in nine starts -- this year.
away_pitcher_note: Myers will make his return to the Phillies' rotation in the pressure-filled atmosphere of Shea Stadium. Myers was optioned to the Minor Leagues last month to rediscover his fastball and swagger, which the righty feels he's accomplished. He made four starts at three levels, with positive results. He has not faced the Mets this season.

home_pitcher_note: The modest requirements of a quality start suggest Perez pitched well against the Reds Saturday night. He surrendered three runs, two earned, in six innings. But he emerged as the losing pitcher and not only because the Mets' offense fell short behind him. Perez walked successive batters to start the fourth; the first base runner scored. He later surrendered a go-ahead, two-out single to the No. 8 hitter. Facing a batting order with four left-handed hitters, he retired the side in order once. But now he has four straight quality starts -- and a .500 record.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer is coming off another masterful outing against the Marlins, as he limited them to two runs in six innings. The 45-year-old lefty has been equally impressive against the Mets this season, posting a 3.37 ERA against them in three outings.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey's streak of consecutive starts won ended at six in Cincinnati on Sunday, but he didn't lose, and he provided what few of his starting colleagues provide -- length. He pitched seven innings and allowed only six hits and a walk. But three of the hits were solo home runs, a surprising development because he had surrendered merely four home runs in 108 2/3 innings before Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Boggs, a rookie, won three of his first five Major League starts but then ran into a problem against the Mets on July 3: he allowed 11 runs -- 10 of them earned -- on 10 hits and six walks in six innings.
summary: 2008-07-25 - St. Louis Cardinals (2) @ New York Mets (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: A former pitching prospect in the Yankees system, Knight will make his first Major League start -- and his first big league appearance in six years -- against the Cardinals Saturday. Knight, the reigning Pacific Coast League Pitcher of the Week, was 5-1 with a 1.60 ERA for Triple-A New Orleans. He last pitched Saturday, striking out 12 batters over six scoreless innings to record the win. Knight briefly considered retiring from baseball this offseason before latching on with the Somerset (N.J.) Patriots of the Atlantic League, and, ultimately, with the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro must figure out how to avoid the big inning. Whether it's because of concentration lapses, mechanical flaws or something else, he's been extremely prone to "crooked numbers" lately. In four of his past five starts, he's had at least one inning in which he allowed at least three runs. The other start in that span? Six and a third shutout. You do the math.
summary: 2008-07-26 - St. Louis Cardinals (10) @ New York Mets (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Re-establishing himself after a five-run shelling in Cincinnati, Santana pitched well enough in Tuesday's game against the Phillies to win. But it didn't work out that way. He pitched eight innings, allowing eight hits and striking out four, holding Philadelphia to two runs. Regardless, a ninth-inning implosion by the Mets bullpen stained a potential victory and produced a no-decision for Santana. Next up, the Cardinals, whom Santana hasn't faced.
away_pitcher_note: For six innings, Lohse turned in a special performance against the Brewers on Tuesday. But as he admitted, it's a nine-inning game, not six. Perfect through four innings, Lohse unraveled in the seventh and eighth innings, allowing the Brewers to come back from a 3-0 deficit and eventually win the game in the ninth. Still, Lohse has been the Cardinals' most efficient pitcher this year possessing excellent stuff en route to a 12-2 record. Two wins short of tying a career-high for a season, Lohse has pitched into the seventh inning for five straight games.
summary: 2008-07-27 - St. Louis Cardinals (1) @ New York Mets (9) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco took his second straight loss against the Braves on Wednesday, giving up five runs -- the most he had given up since June 5 against the Braves -- on eight hits in five innings. Nolasco ended up striking out three and walking three before leaving with 84 pitches under his belt. Nolasco has struggled since going on a five-game winning streak between June 10 and July 7 -- when he posted a 1.83 ERA in five starts. Since the All-Star break, he has given up nine runs in 12 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Maine finally got through the seventh inning Wednesday -- a feat he hadn't attained since May 7 -- allowing three runs, striking out five and walking two against the Phillies. His pitch count reached the century mark once again (104), but he stretched those tosses through seven, and, of the six hits he allowed, most of the damage came on back-to-back home runs in the second inning. He'll now face the Marlins, whom he has yet to face this season.

home_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old lefty was hurt by the big inning in his last start, a loss against the Cubs at Wrigley Field. A four-run fifth inning put him in a bind. He was hurt by two homers, and he's allowed at least one home run in five straight starts. In that span, opponents have collected eight homers. Olsen suffered his first loss since June 17. He had been 2-0 with three no-decisions over that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Perez held the Phillies to one run through 7 2/3 innings Thursday, further cementing his lore as a big-game pitcher with 12 strikeouts -- six with Ryan Howard and Chase Utley in the batter's box. Even though he finished with a no-decision, Perez wielded an almost unhittable slider and an accurate fastball for most of the afternoon until he plunked Howard in the eighth, loading the bases and prompting a call to the bullpen. The Marlins last saw Perez on May 28 -- prior to his recent successes -- hammering the southpaw for five runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old continues to make steady progress in his comeback from Tommy John elbow ligament replacement surgery. Johnson has made three starts, and in all three games, the right-hander was not involved in the decision. Johnson gave up two homers at Wrigley Field, the first two he has allowed this season. The last time Johnson faced the Mets was on Sept. 12, 2006, at Dolphin Stadium. In that game, he sat through more than 80 minutes of a rain delay, and he left after five innings with forearm stiffness. That was the beginning of his arm problems.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey continued his streak of impressive pitching performances with another solid outing Friday night. He threw seven innings of one-run ball and limited the Cardinals to seven hits, striking out five. The right-hander did not walk a single batter and has recorded only one walk in his last four starts. Pelfrey said the command on his breaking ball is still not where he wants it to be, but it's getting better. He has now won seven of his last eight starts. He has not lost since May 26 against Florida when he exited after just four innings. Pelfrey is 0-1 with a 9.00 ERA against the Marlins this season.

home_pitcher_note: Backe had a decent start in his last time out, earning a no-decision in the Astros' 6-4 loss to the Brewers. The Houston offense had a tough time at the plate with runners on base, scoring just four runs in support of Backe even though they racked up 14 hits. Backe will be making his firsts start of the season against the Mets and has historically doesn't have much experience against them, going 1-1 with a 4.41 ERA against New York over the last three seasons.
away_pitcher_note: Manager Jerry Manuel is hoping that Martinez -- who has been grieving his father's death in the Dominican -- can be ready to start the opening game of the Astros series Friday. By then, his time on the bereavement list will have passed, and Manuel hopes to have Martinez pitching against Minor League hitters in Port St. Lucie or with the Mets in Miami. If he pitches on Tuesday, Martinez will be ready for a Friday start, and if the warm-up session is moved to Wednesday, Johan Santana can move up to Friday and let Martinez slide back to Saturday. Martinez hasn't pitched since before the All-Star break when he tweaked his right groin in a four-inning, zero-run affair against the Rockies July 12.

home_pitcher_note: Assuming Oswalt stays on his regular schedule with four days of rest between starts, he'll take the hill for the middle game against the Mets. Oswalt won his last outing in his first start back from the disabled list, topping the Reds after allowing four runs over five innings. Oswalt compiled a 1-1 record and a 4.50 ERA over two starts against the Mets in 2007. In his career versus the Mets, Oswalt is 5-4 with a 3.52 ERA over 11 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Santana pitched the Mets' first complete game since Oliver Perez turned one in in 2006, allowing six hits and one run to the Cardinals on Sunday. He faced the minimum through the first four innings, and Santana's lone blemish came on a solo home run in the seventh inning. After taking some heat for bowing out before the ninth inning in a start against the Phillies, Santana demanded the ball in the final frame and finished with 118 pitches -- three above the number manager Jerry Manuel had in mind. In five innings at Minute Maid Park, Santana has allowed one career run.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf will slide in behind Oswalt, which means he gets an extra two days of rest before this start. Wolf made his Astros debut in Milwaukee on July 27, allowing four runs (three earned) over 4 1/3 innings. Wolf faced the Mets once this year while with the Padres, allowing one run over seven inning in a winning effort. Wolf has good career numbers against the Mets -- 10 wins, 5 losses and a 3.35 ERA over 26 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Because the Mets scratched John Maine from Sunday's start with a mild strain of his right rotator cuff, Perez will take his turn in the rotation. Perez, thanks to an off-day on Thursday, will pitch on regular rest. Despite the relative brevity of his outing last Tuesday -- he had lasted at least seven innings in three of his previous five starts -- Perez was every bit as effective as he has been in recent weeks. Over his six most recent outings, Perez has posted a 1.36 ERA with 44 strikeouts and 15 walks.

home_pitcher_note: Though he entered Wednesday's game against the Marlins with wins in each of his previous seven decisions, Pelfrey could not last more than four innings at Dolphin Stadium. Six hits in the fourth inning -- four of them for extra bases -- combined to knock Pelfrey out of the game after only 78 pitches. He allowed five runs in total, striking out three and walking none. Pelfrey's next start comes against the Padres, a team he held to one run in six innings last month in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Young looked sharp in his last start on July 29 which just so happened to be his first start since May 21 when he took an Albert Pujols line drive off his face. Young, who needed two surgeries to repair facial fractures and a deviated septum, struck out six of the first seven Arizona hitters he faced. All told, he struck out eight in five innings -- he was on a pitch count of roughly 90 pitches -- and allowed two hits and two walks in five scoreless innings.
summary: 2008-08-05 - San Diego Padres (5) @ New York Mets (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Though the Mets entered last Friday's game with thoughts of keeping Martinez somewhere between 70-80 pitches, they allowed him to throw 87 of them against the Astros before calling it a night. That was enough for Martinez to complete five innings, keeping his Mets in the game in the process. Martinez allowed three runs on five hits -- though three of them were home runs. The start was his first in three weeks, after taking time off to nurse a groin injury and attend his father's funeral.
away_pitcher_note: Cha Seung Baek had a solid start going until he ran into a fifth-inning jam that saw him give up four runs (three earned) on four hits while throwing 31 pitches. The defense behind him didn't help him much in producing two errors, but catcher Josh Bard said that Baek "kept competing." Baek, who hasn't seen the seventh inning in his last seven starts continued an up-and-down season that has seen him show flashes but not on a consistent basis for the Padres. He currently carries a 3-6 record and 5.22 ERA into his next start.
summary: 2008-08-06 - San Diego Padres (4) @ New York Mets (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Santana was perfect for the first three innings of Saturday's start in Houston, but he hit pockets of trouble the rest of the way. So with an ever-rising pitch count and an Astros rally in the works, Santana left after 6 1/3 innings, having allowed one run, three hits and two walks. He struck out three, but lost a sure victory when Billy Wagner blew the save. Against the Padres, his next opponent, Santana is 1-2 lifetime with a 2.89 ERA. He allowed one run in the latter of those losses, back in early June.
away_pitcher_note: Even with a potential Cy Young award winner in the Giants' Tim Lincecum on the other side in his last start, the Padres' young stud Banks held his own, allowing two runs (one earned) on eight hits in seven innings on 88 pitches. Banks also recorded his fourth quality start of the season and is 1-0 in his last four starts.
summary: 2008-08-07 - San Diego Padres (3) @ New York Mets (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Manager Jerry Manuel would have preferred to use Perez on Saturday on an extra day of rest, but the absence of disabled righty John Maine and the fact that Perez threw merely 77 pitches in his most recent start, on Sunday in Houston, prompted the manager to change his thinking. Perez will start on Friday against the team he has beaten twice in three starts this season. He has a 2-2  record -- but the Mets' record is 5-2 -- in his seven most recent starts. His ERA in that period is 1.97.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco was pretty close to a complete game in a win against the Rockies on Saturday, but he'll settle for a solid eight-inning effort. Nolasco gave up three runs off four hits while striking out a career-high 13 batters and walking none. The 25-year-old's only flaw was not being able to figure out Matt Holliday, who was responsible for two of the runs and three of the hits. Other than that, and a 22-pitch first inning that saw him give up a run, Nolasco was unhittable. He finished retiring the last seven hitters in order and threw 93 pitches. It was his first win in five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Brian Stokes, who has spent all of his 2008 season with the Triple-A New Orleans Zephyrs, will start in place of the injured John Maine. Stokes, 30 next month and in his ninth season as a professional, has a 3-7 big league record, achieved with the Rays in 2006 and last year. His record with the Zephyrs is 10-8. He has a 4.41 ERA in 23 games -- 22 starts -- and 130 2/3 innings. The Mets limited his pitches in his start Wednesday to make him a viable option.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen pitched a six-inning gem on Sunday against the Rockies, but he had to settle for his 11th no-decision of the season after the Marlins' bullpen allowed three runs in the last three innings. Olsen had a no-hitter going through five and finished the day allowing just one hit -- an infield single by the second hitter he faced in the sixth inning -- while walking two and striking out six. But Olsen's biggest enemy was his pitch count, and it reached 94 by the time he finished the sixth. And with the bases loaded and two outs in the bottom half, the Marlins were looking to add to their two-run lead and were forced to pinch-hit for their starter.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey picked up his 10th win in a solid performance against the Padres on Tuesday night, holding San Diego to two runs through 6 2/3 innings. He scattered nine hits and struck out three, with one walk. It took Pelfrey some time to settle back into a groove after he gave up big hits, though. The righty surrendered two home runs and each was followed by two consecutive singles from the Padres. He said he has continued to struggle with his sinker since the All-Star break, but Pelfrey worked his way out of jams with runners in scoring position. He hasn't found success against the Marlins yet this season, going 0-2 in two starts against Florida, but he will get another chance Sunday afternoon.
away_pitcher_note: During his last start on Tuesday against Philadelphia, Johnson not only moved the Marlins to 5-0 in games he starts this season, he beat a pitcher who was a perfect 10-0 in his career against Florida. Johnson pitched six shutout innings, giving up just five hits and walking four while striking out three before exiting with 97 pitches -- 55 for strikes -- to beat Phillies left-hander Jamie Moyer. Johnson is now 2-0 in his last two starts. In his only start against the Mets this season, he got the win after giving up four runs in 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez settled down after a shaky start on Wednesday night against the Padres. The righty gave up a home run on the first pitch of the game, then surrendered another just two batters later to put the Mets in an early hole. But he retired the next eight batters he faced and allowed just two more hits through 6 1/3 innings. He exited the game after throwing 102 pitches in just his second game since July 12. Martinez was tagged for three runs (two earned) with three strikeouts and three walks. Despite the loss, the righty said he has been able to make adjustments and improve through his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Duke posted one of his best performances of the season his last time out, though he suffered his sixth straight loss, with Brandon Webb going the distance against him in a 3-1 Arizona win. Duke finished seven innings and allowed just four hits, while striking out a season-high six. The two-run homer he gave up proved to be the difference in the game. The outing was a much-needed step in the right direction for Duke, who had given up at least five runs in each of his last five starts. Duke is 2-0 with a 1.77 ERA in three career starts against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Perez had another impressive performance last Thursday in game two of a doubleheader against Colorado. He threw six innings of two-run baseball, complete with just one walk and one strikeout. Perez threw 96 pitches, 62 for strikes, as the Nationals picked up a 6-3 win over Colorado to sweep the doubleheader before leaving for Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Santana pitched well against the Padres on Thursday, but his 10th win eluded him again as the Mets' bullpen could not hold onto his lead. The lefty gave up just four hits through seven-plus innings and held San Diego to two runs, recording seven strikeouts with three walks. Santana left the game after throwing 104 pitches -- his fourth straight start that he has surpassed the 100-pitch mark. He has consistently left his team in a position to win, but Santana has suffered tough luck losses this season. Thursday marked the sixth time the bullpen has cost him a victory. Santana gave up just two runs on seven hits through seven innings in his last start against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Bergmann pitched a gem in the first game of a doubleheader in Colorado on Thursday, going seven innings and allowing only Matt Holliday's solo home run, which drove him from the game. For his part, Bergmann threw just 102 pitches -- 64 for strikes -- and fanned seven batters in the 6-3 Washington win.
away_pitcher_note: Maine, fully healed from a strained right rotator cuff, will come off the disabled list in time for his next time around in the Mets' rotation, putting him back into the No. 2 starter role. His last outing, on July 28, was cut short to 4 1/3 innings due to stiffness in that shoulder, even though he surrendered one earned run and struck out six Marlins before exiting. Fully confident in both his fastball but still working the rust off his offspeed pitches heading into this matchup with the Nationals, Maine carries a career 5-2 record with a 4.44 ERA vs. them into Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Balester turned in another good performance in his last start against the Brewers, allowing just four runs, three earned. He went five innings and struck out four, but the Nationals were shut down by Milwaukee hurler CC Sabathia and Balester picked up the loss, his fourth of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Perez threw seven scoreless innings Friday, holding the Marlins to two hits and striking out eight. His slider hit every spot he aimed for, starting it over the plate and having it slide in toward right-handed batters, and Perez's fastball showed a tremendous amount of life at 95 mph. But it was also a taxing outing, robbing Perez's arm of 120 pitches. With the win, he moved to 7-0 against winning teams, but now he faces the Nationals, who are last in the National League East. On April 24, his first and only outing against Washington this year, he allowed five runs in 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: If Pirates manager John Russell wants to stick with Davis, he'll get the go on Friday when the Bucs host the New York Mets. Davis did well in his first start this season for the Pirates, on Sunday at Philadelphia. He surrendered two runs, both unearned, on four hits. Though he took a no-decision, he displayed good velocity on his fastball over six innings and showed a decent slider. Prior to the Sunday's start, Davis had pitched seven innings out of the bullpen, giving up two runs.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey was pulled on Sunday after allowing six runs in 4 2/3 innings against the Marlins, struggling with his command by matching his three strikeouts with three walks and a hit batsman. The first, second and third innings were a setback, but the fourth and fifth were his undoing, as he faced 15 batters who accounted for four of his earned runs. In three appearances against the Marlins this season, Pelfrey has surrendered 15 runs in 12 2/3 innings. Next, he'll take on the Pirates, whom he has never faced.

home_pitcher_note: Duke settled into a rhythm after getting off to a shaky start against the Mets on Monday afternoon. Duke was tagged for five runs (three earned) and gave up two homers, but most of his struggles came in the first three innings, and the lefty kept his team in the game long enough to come away with a no-decision. He gave up eight hits, striking out three, with one walk. Duke remains 2-0 in four career starts against the Mets, and he will get the chance to improve that record on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez sustained a Mets lead through six innings against the Pirates on Monday, holding them to one run and three hits. Four walks opposed to three strikeouts put Martinez in a couple tough spots, but he worked his way out of jams with a timely changeup and a fastball that peaked at 90 mph in the latter innings. He'll face the Pirates again, this time on the road at PNC Park, one of three ballparks where Martinez has yet to allow a home run in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Despite giving up two early home runs against the Reds in his last start, Karstens proved he could bounce back from adversity with a strong seven-inning performance. The outing came four days after his shutout at Arizona. Despite his first loss as a Pirate, manager John Russell liked how the right-hander kept attacking hitters and sticking with stuff. Karstens will go for win No. 3 against a Mets squad he has yet to face in his short career.
away_pitcher_note: Santana picked up his 10th win of the season Tuesday night with a strong performance against Washington. The lefty went seven innings, striking out six and allowing just three runs while walking two. He scattered eight hits over the start, throwing just 94 pitches, 65 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm has taken hold of that "ace" label and run with it. The lefty allowed two runs in eight innings his last time out and has now pitched through the sixth inning in 18 consecutive starts. He's allowed two or fewer runs in seven of his last nine. The consistency of all four of Maholm's pitches continues to improve, and as a result, he's maintaining great efficiency. Not to mention he threw 22 first-pitch strikes in his last start. Maholm is 3-1 with a 2.16 ERA in four career starts against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Maine was in command in his first start back from right rotator cuff soreness. Over five innings, the right-hander struck out six and allowed just one hit and no runs. He walked four before giving way to the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: Perez continued to impress with his last outing, a three-run, eight strikeout affair. The left-hander tossed 6 2/3 innings of scoreless baseball before tiring and allowing three Nationals to score, cuing his exit from the game. The New York bullpen held up, though, and Perez got more than enough run support in a 9-3 victory.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes has proven he can be effective at the Triple-A level, having gone 1-1 with a 2.31 ERA in eight starts for Richmond this year. But when the 23-year-old southpaw is brought back up to make this start, he'll have to show the consistent control that he lacked in 15 starts for the Braves earlier this year. In his past six big league appearances (five starts), he went 0-5 with an 8.74 ERA.  Opponents produced a .451 on-base percentage during that span.

home_pitcher_note: The Mets have won 11 of Pelfrey's past 13 starts, and he's won nine of them. Now, he faces the team that beat him twice in his first eight starts. His ERA in 9 1/3 innings against the Braves this season is 10.61. Pelfrey has a 6-5 record at Shea Stadium that belies his 2.81 ERA there. He has allowed three home runs in 83 1/3 innings at home, one by Kelly Johnson. Chipper Jones hit one against him in Atlanta. Brian McCann has a .545 batting average, a .615 on-base percentage and a .909 slugging percentage in 13 career plate appearances against Pelfrey.
away_pitcher_note: Despite losing four of his first six starts since the All-Star break, Jurrjens has produced a 3.57 ERA. He recorded a career-high nine strikeouts and received just one of support in Friday's loss to the Giants. The rookie right-hander says he's not fatigued, despite the fact that he's surpassed his previous career-high innings total. Some of his recent struggles have been the result of an inconsistent changeup. He is 2-0 with a 2.77 ERA in two starts against the Mets this year.

home_pitcher_note: His record over .500 and his ERA lower than 5.00 for the first time this season, Martinez has a chance to accomplish something that has been beyond him since his first two starts last season -- win successive starts. He completed seven innings against the offensively challenged Pirates on Saturday night; that was a 2008 first for him. And he has allowed merely four earned runs in his past three starts (19 1/3 innings). He hasn't faced the Braves since Sept. 27, 2006, when he tore his right rotator cuff while striking out Scott Thorman.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton will be attempting to win consecutive starts for the first time in more than three years. Since ending a three-year injury-induced absence from the mound, the 35-year-old southpaw has progressively gained confidence in his health and pitches. He had his sinker working on Saturday, when he induced 10 ground-ball outs in six innings against the Giants. Hampton is motivated by the fact that he must prove himself before his contract expires at the end of the season.

home_pitcher_note: The overstated, unrealistic expectations the public developed when the Mets acquired Santana were met on Sunday, when the left-hander shut out the Pirates on three hits and no walks. Santana managed that partially because the young Pirates hitters weren't particularly selective about Santana's pitches and because plate umpire Ed Hickox had a strike zone that would have been the envy of Tom  Glavine and other strike-zone stretchers. Santana threw 113 pitches, few of them stressful, in pitching his fifth big league shutout. Next, he faces the team he opposed on Aug. 2. That start produced a no-decision in a 10-inning Mets loss. Santana allowed one run on three hits and two walks in 6 1/3 innings in the outing.
away_pitcher_note: Astros manager Cecil Cooper called Oswalt's last start the second-best outing he has seen from the ace. In the start, Oswalt one-hit the Diamondbacks over eight innings. The right-hander struck out 10, tying his season high, and walked two. He gave up four runs on six hits in his previous start against New York, taking a no-decision over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Maine's sore shoulder is likely to limit him to about 100 pitches per start. And pitching coach Dan Warthen says Maine's fastball likely will be compromised for the rest of the season. Maine has pitched five innings in each of his last two starts and has exceeded five once in six starts. He hasn't faced the Astros this season.
away_pitcher_note: Backe's rollercoaster season took another nose dive in his last start, when he gave up 11 runs on nine hits in 5 1/3 innings against the Diamondbacks. Backe has shown control at times and lacked command at others, so the Astros aren't quite sure what they will get from start to start. He got a no-decision in his last start against the Mets this season, giving up three runs on 10 hits in six innings, and he is 1-2 all time against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Perez pitched through control problems on Tuesday but managed to hold the Mets within range, allowing three runs to the Braves in 6 1/3 innings. Five walks proved his lack of command in the no-decision, but manager Jerry Manuel could still say after the game that Perez is one of his most consistent starters. All of the damage came in the third inning after Perez loaded the bases with no outs. But he'd survive, handing off to Mexican countryman Luis Ayala in the seventh inning with two on. He'll next face the Astros, against whom he holds a 2-2 record with a 3.31 ERA in 35 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf was ineffective in his last outing, allowing six earned runs over four innings in a loss to the Brewers. He yielded five runs in the fourth inning, including a two-run single to pitcher CC Sabathia. Wolf, a former Phillie, has extensive experience against the Mets. This year, he's 2-0 against them with a 0.75 ERA, having yielded one run over 13 innings. Lifetime versus the Mets, he's 11-5 with a 3.25 ERA over 27 games, all starts.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey put aside manager Jerry Manuel's concerns that the 24-year-old would tire late in the season, surviving all nine innings Wednesday and holding the Braves to three runs on three hits. After loading the bases in the sixth, Pelfrey maturely utilized the hard sink on his pitches to induce a key double play ball, limiting the inning's run total to two. Pelfrey said after the game that he was more efficient because he was marking the catcher's glove at precise locations rather than firing it in toward the plate, throwing 62 of his 108 pitches for strikes Wednesday. While he didn't face the Astros during the two teams' last encounter, he has struggled against them with a 6.32 ERA in 15 2/3 career innings.
away_pitcher_note: Despite feeling off mechanically, Moehler earned his ninth win of the season in his last start, holding the Brewers to two runs (one earned) over 5 1/3 innings to extend his winning streak to five. The right-hander hasn't lost since July 4 and since then has logged five wins and three no-decisions. Moehler last faced the Reds in Cincinnati on Aug. 9, when he allowed one run over seven innings in a winning effort.

home_pitcher_note: The 22-year veteran ran his streak of allowing three runs or fewer to 14 with a fine effort against Washington. In that game, he surrendered one earned run in 6 2/3 innings, but he received a no-decision. In 18 career starts against the Mets this season, the lefty is 7-4 with a 2.85 ERA. He has faced them four times this season, giving up three, two, two and one run in those outings.
away_pitcher_note: By the time Martinez handed the ball to manager Jerry Manuel with one on and no outs in the eighth inning Thursday, his veteran trickery had worn out against the Braves, who tacked on four runs in seven innings. Manuel doesn't foresee Martinez, whose fastball is consistently working in the mid-80s mph, to last more than a couple of rotations through an opponent's lineup. But Martinez seemingly surpassed those expectations, striking out six, taking the mound to start the eighth, and surpassing 100 pitches. In his last outing in Philadelphia, Martinez allowed two earned runs in 5 1/3 innings and won.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick is still fighting the ups and downs that come with a hurler's first full season in the Major Leagues, but showed significant progress Friday against the Dodgers. The 23-year-old went 5 2/3 innings, allowing three hits and walking two to earn the victory. The win came on the heels of a six-start stretch in which Kendrick recorded a 6.90 ERA to raise his season mark to 5.01. He is now in a three-way tie with Jamie Moyer and Cole Hamels for the team lead in wins. In three career starts against the Mets, Kendrick is 1-1 with a 2.40 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Santana delivered another impressive performance on Friday night, posting seven shutout innings against the Astros. It marked the second straight game that Santana held opponents scoreless, bringing his streak to 16 innings. His pitch count built up to a career-high 121, but he has thrown six innings or more in his last seven starts, including two complete games. He bounced back after early struggles led to 62 pitches through the first three innings. Santana scattered eight hits, striking out five with one walk. He has not recorded a loss since June 28, and he has limited opponents to three runs or fewer in nine of his last ten games.

home_pitcher_note: The 21-year-old will have a big test in the series opener with New York. Volstad deserved a better fate in his last start, a loss at Arizona. In 5 1/3 innings, he allowed four runs, but with a break from his defense, he probably could have escaped with just two runs allowed. Volstad has logged 50 innings in his rookie career, with just two home runs allowed. In nine MLB appearances, and eight starts, Volstad has struck out 32 and walked 23. He's given up 48 total hits.
away_pitcher_note: John Maine will miss his scheduled start Friday after being placed on the 15-day disabled list Monday with a bone spur in his right shoulder. A day off Thursday gives the Mets options and manager Jerry Manuel said it will allow them to go without a fifth starter until Sept. 2. Perez will likely start in Maine's spot Friday, going on regular rest. Against the Astros on Sunday, Perez allowed four runs in 6 1/3 innings. He flashed his mid-90s fastball with eight strikeouts. Perez held the Marlins scoreless through seven innings in his previous start against Florida on Aug. 8.

home_pitcher_note: On a roll, Nolasco returns home after two dominating performances out West. The 25-year-old followed up his two-hit shutout in San Francisco by limiting the D-backs to three hits and two runs in 7 1/3 innings at Chase Field. In those two games, Nolasco combined to strike out 21 and walk two, while allowing five hits and two runs in 16 1/3 innings. With 13 wins, Nolasco has established a career high in victories, and he's won three of his past four decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey continued his recent dominance with his second straight complete-game performance on Monday night. He came within two outs of a shutout before the Astros scored their first run of the night. Pelfrey scattered six hits and struck out six without recording a walk. A few weeks earlier, manager Jerry Manuel had expressed interest in giving Pelfrey some extra rest because of the high number of innings he has piled up, but the young pitcher has been economical with his pitches, holding his pitch count total to just 108 through his nine innings Monday. The Marlins have been Pelfrey's one weak spot this season. He is 0-3 with a 10.66 ERA against the Fish.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, against the Braves on Tuesday, Olsen had a rough first inning but rolled the rest of the way in his 5 1/3-inning outing, which resulted in a no-decision after Atlanta pulled off a four-run ninth inning in a walk-off win. In the first inning, Olsen gave up three quick runs, and that eventually led him to a high pitch count, which resulted in his ninth outing of less than six innings. Olsen finished off having allowed four runs on five hits while walking three and striking out three. He left after throwing 103 pitches and got his 13th no-decision of the year despite leaving with a 6-4 lead.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez gave up one run through the first four innings on Tuesday, holding the Phillies at bay as the Mets surged past them. But the fifth inning ruined the veteran's night, upping his total earned runs allowed to five. He escaped with a no-decision, eight strikeouts and two walks, and, though the Mets led when he left the game, the bullpen was unable to hold the lead. Martinez also pushed his arm with 110 pitches, 69 for strikes. Next are the Marlins, whom he faced April 1, allowing four runs in 3 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets was backed into a corner in his last start but managed to toss six scoreless innings, working his way out of more than a few jams in the early innings. He struck out twice as many batters has he walked and yielded only five hits against St. Louis. Sheets went as far as six innings all six of his August starts and will try to continue the longevity vs. the Mets, against whom he is 4-2 with a 5.10 ERA in his career.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies were effective in either fouling off Santana's pitches or taking them over the fence, forcing the Mets ace out of the game after six innings with six strikeouts and three runs allowed in a no-decision. He threw 106 pitches, 67 for strikes, and gave up two home runs to end his scoreless innings streak at 16. Next are the Brewers, who Santana has a 3-2 career record against with 3.61 ERA in 47 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Parra's six quality innings last week in St. Louis went for naught, as the Brewers' bullpen gave up four runs in the eighth inning. He's been just as consistent as all of the Brewers' other starters this year and has made many forget that this is only his second year in the big leagues. This will be the second start of Parra's career against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: In the absence of John Maine, who hit the disabled list last week with a bone spur in his right shoulder, the Mets will turn to their top pitching prospect, Niese. Relying on his signature 12-to-6 curveball, Niese posted an 11-8 record and a 3.13 ERA between Double-A Binghamton and Triple-A New Orleans this season -- and after joining the Zephyrs, he lost only once in seven starts. Technically, Niese will be starting on short rest, having pitched on Friday night in New Orleans. But he threw only 65 pitches in that outing, meaning he should be fresh for his Major League debut.

home_pitcher_note: Bush was caught in a heated pitching duel with Pirates starter Tom Gorzelanny on Friday, but Bush was able to escape PNC Park with his ninth win of the year. The quality outing also improved his August record to 4-0. Bush continues to show signs of improvement on the road and is gaining more and more confidence from his manager, Ned Yost. Bush will attempt to keep the good vibrations going against the Mets, whom he is 1-2 with a 3.86 ERA against in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Despite walking five batters on Friday against the Marlins, Oliver Perez allowed only two runs, but he could not muster a win. The five walks weren't even the trouble -- a solo homer, an error and a sacrifice fly amounted for all the damage off Perez. But it was enough. Perez now hasn't won in three starts, marking his longest streak since early June. He'll look to right himself against the Brewers, who tagged him for six runs in 4 1/3 innings back in April.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey's bid for a third consecutive complete game fell 2 1/3 innings short last Saturday in Miami, as did his bid for a fourth straight win. But the Mets certainly had no qualms with the way Pelfrey pitched. The two runs he allowed would have been enough to win on many other nights, and his inefficiency -- 99 pitches through six innings, and 116 through 6 2/3 -- was an aberration in the context of the month. Pelfrey completed August with a 4-1 record and 2.93 ERA, and will commence September against the Phillies, whom he has beaten once in two attempts.
away_pitcher_note: Myers continued his second-half turnaround with a dominating win over the Cubs on Saturday afternoon. Against the best offense in the National League, Myers tossed seven-plus innings of two-run ball. He gave up 11 hits (all singles), walked none and struck out eight. At one point, the right-hander retired 11 hitters in a row. Myers is 5-1 with a 1.78 ERA since the All-Star break. Only two other pitchers, both acquired in July trades, boast better ERAs during the second half. The Brewers' C.C. Sabathia (6-0, 1.41) and the Cubs' Rich Harden (4-1, 1.66) have received widespread attention for helping their teams in the playoff push.

home_pitcher_note: Despite allowing the Marlins just two runs last Sunday, Martinez needed 101 pitches to do so. And so he lasted only six innings in Miami, striking out four and walking one. The outing was the third straight in which Martinez had thrown more than 100 pitches, after doing so just once in his previous five starts. And his season high in pitches, 111, also came last week against the Phillies, whom he will face on Saturday. Martinez is 3-2 against the Phillies since joining the Mets in 2005.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer held the Cubs to two earned runs in 5 1/3 innings to earn his team-leading 12th victory Sunday against the Cubs. He has been the Phils' most consistent starting pitcher this season, holding opponents to three earned runs or fewer in 15 of his past 16 starts. Moyer is 1-1 with a 4.40 ERA in five starts against the Mets this year.

home_pitcher_note: Santana once again pitched well enough to win Monday, when he threw six good, not great, innings against the Brewers. But he came away with an ERA one point higher than it had been, and this piece of self-satisfaction -- the Mets have a 9-3 record in his 12 most recent starts and are unbeaten in his past six. He struck out 10, equaling his high for the season, walked one and allowed seven hits. But he was denied a victory by his defense and offense and his own balk. Now he is to oppose the Phillies for the fifth time in his first National League season. Despite a 3.10 ERA in 29 innings against the Phillies, Santana has a 1-0 record is the first four starts. They're batting .213 against him.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels, the Phillies' ace, turned in 7 1/3 innings of shutout ball against the Nationals on Tuesday night in Washington, lowering his ERA to 3.01, his lowest mark since May 20.

home_pitcher_note: Afforded a six-run lead before he threw a pitch, Perez still managed to bring drama to his Wednesday start against the Brewers. Five walks in 6 2/3 innings againt a team with right-handed power will do that. Perez now has walked five in three of his last four starts. The Mets have won three of the four, he has won one. Now he faces the pesky Nats, against whom he has produced mixed results -- a 1-1 record and 5.84 ERA in two starts this season and a 2-2 record with a 5.26 ERA in the preceding three seasons. Good Ollie, Bad Ollie lives. You never know with either. He pulled two 50 mph changeups out of his bag of tricks against the Brewers. His own catcher was way out in front, having called for fastballs.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan had another quality outing his last time out, going six innings and giving up two runs on five hits. It was the top of the third that proved to be his undoing. With two outs, Lannan had a tough time getting the  final out. On a 3-1 pitch, Jimmy Rollins drove in Carlos Ruiz with a single to left and advanced to second on the throw from Willie Harris. Chase Utley followed and was behind in the count 0-2, but Lannan couldn't put him away as Utley singled to left-center to score Rollins.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey delivered a solid performance against the Phillies on Friday, giving up just four hits in seven innings. He recovered quickly after allowing one run to cross the plate in the opening frame. Pelfrey held the Phillies scoreless through the next five innings until he surrendered a two-run homer in the seventh inning, one of his few mistakes of the night. He was tagged for three runs (two earned), striking out four while walking two. It marked his fifth straight start in which he held opponents to three earned runs or fewer. Pelfrey is 1-1 with a 0.69 ERA in two outings against the Nationals. He has given up just one run and eight hits to Washington this season.
away_pitcher_note: Perez will face the Mets for the third time this season. He is 1-1 with a 4.42 ERA against them this season. The last time he faced New York was on Aug. 12. Perez pitched six solid innings, giving up three runs on eight hits. Most importantly, he gave most of the relievers a rest.

home_pitcher_note: Santana stopped the bleeding for the Mets Sunday, holding the Phillies to two runs in 7 1/3 innings following his club's two straight losses to its division rival. He allowed five hits -- one a home run -- striking out six and walking three. Most importantly, the 29-year-old once again extended his arm past 100 pitches, a workload he has surpassed in nine out of his last 10 starts, throwing 71 of his 116 pitches for strikes. While Santana has fared well against the Braves in most statistical categories, holding this National League East opponent to four earned runs in 14 innings, both starts have resulted in tough-luck losses and only four Braves have been struck out by Santana in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton surrendered a career-high four homers while getting a no-decision with a seven-inning effort against the Nationals on Saturday. The sinkerball specialist has been frustrated by the number of pitches he's been leaving up in the zone recently. While he's still showing some rust, the lefty has also steadily proven that he can still be effective at the Major League level. With injury questions still looming, Hampton needs to pitch well over the final weeks to increase the interest he'll gain on the free-agent market this winter.

home_pitcher_note: Niese got knocked around by the Brewers in his Major League debut on Sept. 3, allowing seven hits, four walks and five runs over three-plus innings. Niese said anxiety undermined him in the first inning. He surrendered a home run to Rickie Weeks on his second big league pitch and walked the next two batters. Nine of his first 13 pitches were balls.
away_pitcher_note: On Sunday afternoon, Reyes was in line to earn his first win since June 13 before his bullpen imploded. Still, while limiting the Nationals to one run in six innings, the 23-year-old southpaw provided some reason for optimism. Reyes, who is 0-6 with a 6.90 ERA over his past 10 appearances (nine starts), limited the Mets to two earned runs and four hits in six innings while getting a no-decision at Shea Stadium on Aug. 19.

home_pitcher_note: Perez was roughed up early Tuesday night, giving up seven runs on eight hits in only 3 1/3 innings against the Nationals. It marked his shortest outing since June 2 and just the second time in his last 15 starts that he has not pitched at least six full innings. He struck out three, recording two walks. Until Tuesday, Perez had been consistent for the Mets lately, and he has not recorded a loss since Aug. 3. While his arm strength was there Tuesday, his command and location were not. In his only start against Atlanta this season, Perez held the Braves to three runs on seven hits through 6 1/3 innings to come away with a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Campillo was denied the opportunity to win for the first time in five starts on Tuesday, when the bullpen couldn't hold a ninth-inning lead. Still even while surrendering a pair of homers to the Rockies, the 29-year-old rookie right-hander looked better than he had since his last win on Aug. 8. Because he was facing a new opponent, he was able to utilize his offspeed repertoire effectively. Campillo's first start of the season came on May 20, when he limited the Mets to three hits over six scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: The last time he took the mound, Lannan had one of his worst starts of the season. Against the Mets on Tuesday, the 23-year-old lasted just three innings for the first time since May 2 and gave up five runs on eight hits in the process. After the game, Lannan insisted his arm is fine, even though he's pitched a career-high 163 innings. Over his last five starts, Lannan has posted a 7.82 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing six runs in four innings against the Phillies on Sunday, Martinez said that he had greater flexibility that he had in other recent starts. But the high run total points to a disconnect between physical condition and his performance. He could have escaped Sunday's first start with three runs if not for a few misplays in the outfield. He hasn't opposed the Nationals this season and has had minimal exposure to their regulars in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Perez's worst outing of the season came on Wednesday against the Mets, when he gave up seven runs (six earned) on eight hits in just three innings of work. The six earned runs tied a season high -- which he has set two other times this year -- and over his past seven starts, the 30-year-old has given up 22 runs in 36 2/3 innings (a 5.40 ERA).
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey was credited with a no-decision during the Mets' high-scoring affair with the Nationals on Wednesday, surrendering five runs on eight hits in five innings. Although the duration was less than average -- he hadn't been pulled before the sixth frame since a 4 2/3-inning outing against the Marlins on Aug. 10 -- Pelfrey still threw 96 pitches (56 strikes). His control was streaky, though, especially with Elijah Dukes in the batter's box. Dukes homered in the second inning and was nearly hit in the fourth, causing Dukes to yell at Pelfrey. Dukes was hit by Pelfrey in the fifth, but took first base without incident. Pelfrey will face the Nationals for the fourth time this season in this start, having compiled a 1-1 record against them, with a 2.75 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Martis has had two quality Major League starts in his short career -- and he's got two losses to show for it. His latest was despite giving up two runs (one earned) in five-plus innings against the Marlins on Friday. In his first five innings, Martis -- who allowed two runs in five innings in his Major League debut -- gave up just one run on two hits while striking out nine batters. In the sixth, the Marlins took a 2-1 lead on a Christian Guzman throwing error, and Martis left the game after allowing the first three batters he faced to reach base.
away_pitcher_note: Knight asserted himself in the final four innings he pitched in his lone big league start, against the Cardinals July 26. But that was after he had allowed four runs in the first inning. He has made two one-inning relief appearances and produced uneven results in two Olympic starts. The Nationals' primary hitters are right-handed, which partially explains why Knight was chosen to start. Right-handed hitters are batting .133 against him this season and .281 in his career. Left-handed hitters have batted .462 against him this season and .405 in his career.

home_pitcher_note: It looked like it was going to be a rough night for Redding on Saturday against the Marlins. But after the 30-year-old gave up four runs in the first two innings -- on a couple of two-run shots -- he settled down, keeping the Marlins scoreless on just two hits in his next four innings. With his six-inning performance, the seventh-year veteran set a new career high for innings pitched in a season with 176 1/3. Redding is 1-1 against the Mets this season.
away_pitcher_note: Though Santana's no-decision on Saturday came only after he allowed two straight hits to open the eighth, it was hardly his fault. A shaky bullpen permitted both runs to score, and so Santana was unable to win his seventh straight decision. Pitching with a fastball that he said was "all over the place," Santana did shut out the Braves for seven innings before losing the lead. In two starts against the Nationals this season, he is 2-0 with a 3.21 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes was yanked quickly in Saturday's outing against the Mets, surrendering four earned runs on two home runs in just two innings. The 23-year-old was pinch-hit for in his first chance for an at-bat, making his 37-pitch workload (23 strikes) light yet dubious. He had only one strikeout to offset a two-run home run in the first inning and a solo shot in the second frame. Reyes has lost seven straight decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Partly because it stood in such contrast to his previous start, Perez's outing on Sunday against the Braves proved to be rather encouraging. Perez lasted seven innings, allowing four hits and two runs. He struck out eight batters and walked three. And he did it with the Mets needing a win to maintain an increasing pace in the National League East. Perez's next start will also come against the Braves, whom he has now beaten five times in seven starts over the past two seasons.

home_pitcher_note: Campillo was roughed up early in his fourth consecutive losing decision, allowing four runs -- three earned -- in 3 2/3 innings to the Mets on Sunday. All three earned runs were scored via home runs, the first a solo shot by David Wright in the first inning and the second a two-run homer by Wright in the third. Despite the short outing, Campillo still threw 87 pitches. He'll get another shot at the Mets, who have bested him two out of three times this season.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez has lost three of his last five decisions, and the Mets have lost six of his nine most recent starts. He allowed four runs in six innings against the Nationals on Monday. Armed once again with his cutter -- he hadn't thrown it in his preceding five starts because of a blister on the middle finger of his right hand -- Martinez wasn't sharp. He had gone seven days without pitching, his 18th start pushed back two days because of the rainout Friday. The location of his pitchers was imprecise, especially early. Martinez has faced the Braves once this season. He pitched seven innings in what became a 5-4 Mets victory at Shea Stadium Aug. 21. He allowed four runs in the non-decision, one on a leadoff home run by Yunel Escobar.

home_pitcher_note: Despite allowing four earned runs and 10 hits in 4 1/3 innings against the Phillies on Tuesday, James Parr still drew some postgame praise from manager Bobby Cox, who has been impressed by the rookie hurler's makeup and ability to mix his pitches. The 22-year-old right-hander had tossed six scoreless innings in both of his two previous career starts this month. While enjoying a successful August with Triple-A Richmond and finding some early success at the Major League level, Parr has at least made himself a candidate for Atlanta's 2009 starting rotation.
away_pitcher_note: A double that might have been caught and a four-pitch walk that followed an extended interruption in play were Pelfrey's undoing Tuesday night against the Nationals. Cristian Guzman followed the walk with a booming double to drive in the run in a 1-0 loss. Pelfrey wasn't sharp -- seven hits and four walks in seven innings, but aside from Guzman's hit, he limited the damage. Now he faces the team that has knocked him around a few times this season. He has a 1-2 record and 6.87 ERA in three starts against the Braves. But the losses occurred in April, and he pitched a three-hitter, the first complete game of his career, against them Aug. 20 at Shea Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Niese provided the Mets a signifcant lift when, in his second big league start, he pitched eight shutout innings against the Braves on Sept. 13. His next assignment appears to be a far greater challenge. The Cubs feast on left-handed pitching. They won 29 of their first 44 games in which they were opposed by a left-handed starter. But Niese's curve, the one he threw consistently for strikes -- even when he was behind in the count -- against the Braves, is different from most in the big leagues. It's bigger. The Cubs never have seen it. That's to his advantage -- at least it is the first time through the order.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis is coming off a loss to the Brewers. It was his first start after an extended layoff and affected his ability to find his release point. The end result was five walks, including two in the first which loaded the bases in front of Prince Fielder. That wasn't a good move: Fielder cleared them with a double. Marquis has given up three or fewer runs in four straight starts and walked five for the fifth time this year.

home_pitcher_note: Santana's fine September continued last Thursday in Washington, where he struck out eight Nationals over seven innings, allowing merely one run. That effort earned him a win, which hasn't always been the case this month -- or this year -- when Santana has pitched well. Of his last six no-decisions, all of them have been quality starts. He has produced a 2.68 ERA in those six games, compared to a 1.36 ERA in his six most recent victories. Santana's next start will be his first against the Cubs since holding them to one run over eight innings back in 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Marshall will be making his seventh start as the Cubs adjust their rotation to set it up for the postseason. His last start was Sept. 7 at Cincinnati, when he gave up one run on three hits and two walks over six innings. The lefty is 1-4 with a 4.24 ERA in his six starts, and 2-0 with a 2.81 ERA in 25 relief appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Perez's last outing can be considered a success in at least one respect: He appeared done after five innings and 97 pitches, but gave the Mets an additional effective inning -- his most impressive of the night -- to prevent a shaky bullpen from clocking into work even earlier. Perez still hasn't regained his form from a nearly untouchable July, but he has managed to post two consecutive strong outings, both against the same team -- a not-so-small fact that makes the task tougher. He'll finally face a fresh opponent, the Cubs, on Wednesday, marking his first start against them since 2005.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano lasted 1 2/3 innings in his last start against the Cardinals, much to the disappointment of the 40,000-plus at Wrigley Field. It was his first start since his no-hitter on Sept. 14. Against St. Louis, he gave up eight runs on six hits and three walks over 1 2/3 innings. It was his shortest outing since a 1 1/3-inning start Sept. 4, 2006, against Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez's third straight loss was similar to the one before it, albeit with some slightly better control. The most vexing coincidence was the fact that Martinez again allowed runs in the first inning -- this time, three of them -- and that the Mets never recovered from that deficit. It's a trend that neither Martinez nor manager Jerry Manuel could explain, but that has ruined some otherwise fine outings this season. He'll look to do better against the Cubs, whom he has not faced this decade.
away_pitcher_note: Harden had what he called an "ugly" game against the Brewers. He only gave up one hit over five innings but walked six. He also struck out seven, and had to be pulled because his pitch count had reached 115. Harden had a long layoff before the Milwaukee game because of the Hurricane Ike hiatus, and should do better on a regular routine.

home_pitcher_note: The fact that Mike Pelfrey extended his streak on Sunday to five straight starts without a victory was no fault of his own. Pelfrey allowed only three runs to the Braves over six innings, departing after walking the leadoff man in the seventh. He pitched plenty well enough to win, but another bullpen implosion ensured that Pelfrey would leave with a no-decision. In four starts against the Marlins this season, Pelfrey is 0-3 with a 7.91 ERA -- though his best start against them came earlier this month, when he allowed two runs over 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad gave up three runs (two earned) in five innings during a loss against the Phillies on Sunday. The outing saw the 21-year-old reach a professional high in innings pitched with 169 1/3. Volstad gave up six hits while striking out three and walking two. Two of the runs came on a rare home run. This season, Volstad has only given up three dingers, and in 91 innings for Double-A Carolina, he didn't allow a single long ball. In his only start against the Mets this season, Volstad gave up only one run in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: After days of withholding his Saturday starter, manager Jerry Manuel finally admitted that pitcher "A," the option who would be counted on to throw in the event that the Mets were tied or trailed in the Wild Card, was Johan Santana. The Mets' ace will pitch on three days' rest, a time crunch which is multiplied by the fact that Santana threw a career-high 125 pitches in his last start Tuesday. It was a successful start, though, as Santana limited the Cubs to two runs over eight innings. The only other time Santana has pitched on three days' rest was in Game 1 of the 2004 ALDS, when he allowed one run in five innings against the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco was in line for his 16th win in his last start, but settled for a no-decision after Florida was unable to hold a 4-1 lead in the seventh inning at Cincinnati on Monday. Nolasco allowed three runs on six hits in six-plus innings. The 25-year-old ace of the staff did surpass the 200-innings-pitched mark that day, as he now has 205 1/3 innings. This will be Nolasco's 32nd start, as it winds down his terrific season. Nolasco has struck out 176 and walked 41.

home_pitcher_note: With Johan Santana pitching Saturday, Oliver Perez will also be asked to pitch on three days' rest as the Mets try to make a push for the playoffs. Perez lasted only 4 1/3 innings in his last start Wednesday, allowing five earned runs to the Cubs on six hits and five walks. Against the Marlins, Perez is 3-0 with a 2.03 ERA in 31 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen's hopes of ending the season with a .500 record were shattered when he suffered a loss against the Nationals on Tuesday, giving up four runs (three earned) on eight hits while walking one and striking out two in five innings. Still, 2008 has already seen the 24-year-old reach his career high in innings -- going into his last start with 195 2/3, up from 180 2/3 in 2006 -- and, on Sunday, he'll tie his career high in starts with 33. Over his last five starts, he's 2-3 with a 4.46 ERA (15 earned runs in 30 1/3 innings).
