home_pitcher_note: Lefty Brian Matusz will make one last Grapefruit League start against the Mets on Saturday, before beginning a potential AL Rookie of the Year campaign in Baltimore. Matusz, who has posted a 3.10 ERA in five spring outings to date, will start opposite lefty Oliver Perez.
away_pitcher_note: Niese, who will make his first start of the regular season on Thursday against the Marlins, will be making his final start of Spring Training against the Orioles. Niese has a 5.65 ERA for the spring.

home_pitcher_note: This will be the fifth Opening Day start of Santana's career, his third with the Mets. His record in the first four is 3-1. His ERA in those games is 4.07. He has a 5-1 record and 1.68 ERA in seven career starts (48 1/3 innings) against the Fish. One of the seven was on Opening Day, 2008, his debut with the Mets. Santana allowed, two runs, three hits and two walks in seven innings at Dolphin Stadium. He completed the '08 season with a three-hit shutout of the Marlins at Shea Stadium. Jorge Cantu, Dan Uggla and Cody Ross have hit home runs against Santana. Hanley Ramirez has two singles and six strikeouts in 15 at-bats against the Mets starter. Pitching at Shea Stadium and Citi Field, Santana has produced a 19-6 record and 2.14 ERA in 33 starts and 231 2/3 innings, an average of more than seven innings per start.
away_pitcher_note:
Signed to a four-year, $39 million contract in the offseason, Johnson assumes the role of ace. In 2009, Johnson made his first All-Star appearance, and the 6-foot-7 right-hander established himself as one of the top starters in the National League. He set career highs for wins (15), games started (33) and 
innings pitched (209). The hard-throwing Johnson has made a remarkable comeback from Tommy John surgery in 2007. The past two years, he is 22-6 with a 3.34 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: When the Mets revised the sequence of their rotation, they did so at least partially to spare Mike Pelfrey another start against his primary nemesis team. He has lost his last five decisions against the Marlins and has a 5.40 ERA in his last nine starts against them. But there is more positive reason behind the change as well. Maine has a 5-2 record and 3.12 ERA in 10 career starts against the Marlins. One of his victories came in the 161st game of 2007. He struck out 14 and allowed one infield hit in 7 2/3 shutout innings. Maine has had an unimpressive exhibition season, walking 10 and allowing four home runs and 14 runs in 16 innings. Hanley Ramirez has hit two home runs in 23 at-bats against Maine, and Jorge Cantu has a .400 average in 15 carer at-bats against the Mets' second game starter. Maine has a 7-4 record and 3.16 ERA in 14 starts (82 2/3 innings) in April.
away_pitcher_note:
If he can pick up where he left off in Spring Training, Nolasco is primed for a big season. In 25 1/3 innings of Grapefruit League action, Nolasco walked just one. With command of his fastball and breaking pitches, he is regarded as an upper-level No. 2 starter. Consistency will be key for the 27-year-old, who was Florida's Opening Day starter a year ago. In his final start of 2009, Nolasco struck out a 
franchise-record 16 batters, including a stretch of nine straight. The MLB record is 10 set by Tom 
Seaver.

home_pitcher_note: There is no history here. Jon Niese vs. the Marlins is a clean easel. Niese never has faced the Fish, nor has he made a big league start in April. Hey, for that matter, he's made merely eight starts in the big leagues, and he has faced none of the platers on Marlins roster. What does unfamiliarity breed? The Marlins win 29 of the 51 games in which they were opposed by a left-handed starter last season. But what does that mean now?
away_pitcher_note: Acquired less than a week before Opening Day from the Tigers for prospect Jay Voss, Robertson begins his second stint with the Marlins. The left-hander was drafted by Florida in 1999, and he made his big league debut with the Marlins in 2002. He was traded to Detroit prior to 2003 as part of the deal that brought Mark Redman to Florida. Robertson was slowed by injuries last year, having surgery on his elbow and surgery to repair a torn groin muscle. Initially, Robertson was tabbed as the fifth starter, but he was switched with Anibal Sanchez. Robertson is the lone lefty in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey ducked his least favorite opponent when the sequence of the rotation was changed. Now the Marlins have been replaced by the Nationals as his first 2010 opponent. He has a 3-5 record is 12 career starts against the Nationals, but his ERA in 75 2.3 innings aganust them is 3.72. He has a 4-3 record and 5.92 ERA in 10 starts in April and a 16-18 record in 45 starts in Shea and Citi Field. Pelfrey's performance in spring training was ragged. He has allowed 37 home runs in his career; He allowed seven in a 10 1/3 inning sequence in exhibition games. Josh Willingham, who relishes playing the Mets, has a .412 batting average and two home runs in 17-career at-bats against Pelfrey.
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals decided Saturday that Mock will be their fifth starter to begin the 2010 season. Mock won the job even though he was hit hard in his last two spring starts, including a game against the Astros' Minor League team. He will pitch against the Mets on Friday at Citi Field in his regular-season debut. General manager Mike Rizzo said Mock was picked because of his potential as a starter. The team believes he will one day become a No. 3 starter. Mock was told that he was on a short leash and the club would quickly call up left-hander Scott Olsen if he didn't produce on the mound.

home_pitcher_note: Perez opposed only nine National League opponents last season. The Nationals were one of four teams to face him twice and the only team to beat him twice. He allowed 13 hits and nine walks and hit two batters in only 10 1/3 innings against them. Ollie is not a fast starter. His career ERA in April, 5.92, is higher than his ERA in any other month. He has a 10-15 record in 34 starts in the season's first month. Perez's career record in home starts in 32-35. He won three of five decisions in seven starts at Citi Field last season. Josh Willingham and Adam Dunn have hit three home runs each in 25 and 31 respective career at-bats against Perez.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan is 3-4 with a 3.62 ERA against the Mets during his career. He is looking to atone for his last start, which occurred Monday against the Phillies. It appeared Lannan was going to make up for last year's disappointing Opening Day start against the Marlins. In that game, Lannan lasted three innings and gave up six runs on six hits on the road. But in the top of fourth Monday, Lannan looked like the pitcher who struggled against Florida in last year's opener. Philadelphia batted around and scored five runs. It was Philadelphia's lefty hitters who started things off against Lannan. Chase Utley led off with a walk. On the first pitch Ryan Howard saw from Lannan -- a slider -- he hit a two-run homer over the right-field fence. Lannan faced eight more hitters and allowed three more runs in the inning before he was replaced by left-hander Jesse English, who didn't allow a base runner in 1 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Santana routinely picks on the Nationals, as his 6-1 record and 2.62 ERA against them suggests. Those numbers have been created in a seven-start sequence that has produced 48 innings or almost seven innings per start. Santana has won his five most recent starts against the Nationals, striking out 10 and his 11 in two starts last year. He pitched well enough against the Marlins on Opening Day, allowing one run on four hits and two walks in six innings. His final two innings were not challenging. But the first required 68 pitches. Despite his success against the Nats, Santana has not fared so well against Adam Dunn. The lefthanded-hitting first baseman has four hits in seven career at-bats against Santana, two of them home runs and one of the homers a mammoth jolt that nearly struck what now is the Shea Bridge beyond right center field last season.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez -- who has been working out at the Nationals' complex in Viera, Fla. -- is expected to be activated on Sunday and pitch against the Mets that same day at Citi Field. Hernandez said he will arrive in New York on Saturday. With Hernandez expected to be on the 25-man roster, a reliever must be taken off. The Nationals currently have eight relievers, and manager Jim Riggleman said performance will determine who stays and who goes before Hernandez's arrival on the team.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start since Sept. 27, 2008, while pitching for the Athletics, Smith, who missed last season with various nagging ailments, gave up five runs on four hits (two of them homers) in five innings of a 7-5 road loss to the Brewers. with the exception of three pitches (resulting in two homers and a double), Smith did a reasonable job of hitting his locations, considering how long he had been inactive.
away_pitcher_note: Maine was responsible for one of the two poor starts during the first turn of the Mets rotation. Pitching with a diminished fastball, he needed 92 pitches to achieve 15 outs against the Marlins. And by the point he had thrown his last final pitch, he had allowed eight hits, including two home runs. Maine attributed his performance to poor location of his fastball, but others saw a lack of velocity. He hasn't faced them since June 20, 2008 when he beat them at Coors Field. None of the Rockies have had much exposure to Maine. Todd Helton and Miguel Olivo have eight at-bats each. As was the case last season, Maine was more effective against left-handed hitters than he was against right-handed in his first start.

home_pitcher_note: Cook gave up five runs, four earned, in 5 1/3 innings in a loss to the Brewers in the final game of the season-opening, three-game set. Cook had his sinker working early and threw some effective curveballs. His biggest issue as the game progressed was he got ahead of hitters early in counts but allowed them to extend at-bats. More consistency would put him deeper in games. Cook did not face the Mets last season.
away_pitcher_note: Moved to the third spot in the rotation -- the Mets didn't want John Maine and Ollie Perez next to each other for fear of overworking the bullpen -- Niese responded with a pretty good performance. He appeared quite comfortable as he completed six innings, allowing eight hits, two walks and three runs. The Rockies are one of the eight teams Niese has faced in his brief career. They beat him in the second game of a double header at Citi Field July 30, scoring four runs in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa started 2010 with a dominant one-hit, nine-strikeout performance over seven innings Friday in the home opener, a 9-0 victory over the Padres. De La Rosa is one of those pitchers who, when he's on, you start speaking in whispered tones when the zero in the hit column lasts awhile. All nine strikeouts were on changeups, but pitching coach Bob Apodaca noted, "They were all set up by something early, whether the slider early or definitely fastballs. He was ahead in the count the vast majority of the game." De La Rosa is 3-0 with a 3.71 ERA in eight career games, but just two starts, against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: In his season debut against Washington, Pelfrey displayed all the reasons why the Mets still believe in him (two runs on four hits in six innings) and all the reasons why they remain so frustrated with him (four walks). In the end, it was a victory for Pelfrey -- albeit against a second-rate offense. He'll face a greater test against the Rockies, who battered him for seven runs in four innings in his last trip to Coors Field last September. Pelfrey is 3-2 in five career starts against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: It's far, far too early to be alarmed about Carpenter, but it's not too early to be aware. Carpenter, who allowed seven home runs in the entire 2009 season, has allowed five in two starts. And it could very easily be six, except that Colby Rasmus reached over the wall to rob Scott Rolen in Cincinnati on Opening Day. Carpenter's history suggests he'll get right very quickly, but being susceptible to the long ball is a very unusual trait for the former Cy Young Award winner. He gets the call in the series opener on regular rest, allowing him to pitch five days later in Arizona before the off day.
away_pitcher_note: There was some discussion of skipping Perez's second start of the season, but that would have accomplished little: without an off-day during their road trip to Denver and St. Louis, the Mets would simply be flipping Perez and Johan Santana in the rotation -- not skipping their erratic left-hander altogether. So they are sticking with Perez at Busch Stadium, where he has struggled in the past. In his lone start there last season, Perez allowed four runs in 4 2/3 innings, escaping with a no-decision.
summary: 2010-04-16 - New York Mets (3) @ St. Louis Cardinals (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: There was a lot to like when Garcia last pitched, as the rookie left-hander showed impressive stuff and pretty good command. He looks a great deal different from his first stint in the Majors, back in 2008. The key for Garcia will be to stay healthy, because he's been consistently effective at just about every level. Garcia goes on six days' rest after his first start as the Cardinals take steps to protect him in his first full big league season. He also once again is spared the Sunday night ESPN assignment.
away_pitcher_note: Though Santana didn't pitch particularly poorly in his last start against the Nationals, he complained of a lack of fastball command in the first inning. And he made one bad pitch at precisely the wrong time, resulting in a Josh Willingham grand slam from which he and the Mets never recovered. Though Santana will be pitching at Busch Stadium for the first time in his career, he does have one unenviable piece of history against the Cardinals: Albert Pujols is 6-for-12 with two home runs in his career off Santana.
summary: 2010-04-17 - New York Mets (2) @ St. Louis Cardinals (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: If Wainwright had gotten off to this kind of start last season, he very likely would have won the Cy Young Award rather than finishing third. He's been absolutely outstanding through two starts, quite a turnaround from a somewhat slow beginning to '09. Wainwright is pounding the strike zone, pitching deep into games, getting groundballs and strikeouts -- in short, doing all the things he does when he's at his best. He'll get the call in the Sunday night game, an assignment which shouldn't faze him in the slightest.
away_pitcher_note: Three walks, a hit batsman and a throwing error -- his own throwing error -- led to six runs and an early exit for Maine on Wednesday in Denver. Maine walked two of the three leadoff batters he faced, served up an RBI double to pitcher Greg Smith and allowed eight runs in total, tying his career high. He also vented his frustration with some revealing body language on the mound. Maine will look to improve against the Cardinals, who battered him for five runs (and drew five walks) in 5 2/3 innings in their lone meeting last season.
summary: 2010-04-18 - New York Mets (3) @ St. Louis Cardinals (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Though some defensive blunders undermined Niese last Wednesday in Denver, nothing hurt more than Ryan Spilborgh's three-run homer to the deepest part of Coors Field. Niese allowed nine hits and one walk in total, striking out two. But the Mets could not do nearly enough offensively to turn those numbers into a win. Niese will now open the Mets homestand against the Cubs, the team that handed him the first loss of his Major League career in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Wells did not get a decision in his last start against the Brewers. In that game, he gave up four runs on 10 hits over 6 1/3 innings while striking out seven. The one mulligan Wells would like to have is a walk he issued to pitcher Dave Bush in the fifth. Bush scored that inning on Rickie Weeks' two-run double, which gave the Brewers the lead. He last faced the Mets on Sept. 6 in New York, and took the loss, despite giving up one earned run on seven hits over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Featuring a sharp split-fingered fastball, along with good control of his slider and curve, Mike Pelfrey blanked a potent Rockies offense for seven innings on Thursday in Denver. Continuing to grow more confident in his secondary pitches, Pelfrey is no longer relying solely on his power sinker to generate outs. That much should serve him well against the Cubs, who mustered only one run in eight innings in their lone meeting with Pelfrey last season.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano had to leave his last start because of cramps in his right hand and right calf, and also because he threw 121 pitches over five innings. The Brewers were aggressive and fouled a lot of pitches off, which was part of the reason for the high pitch count. Big Z hasn't thrown that many pitches since he totaled 125 on July 24, 2008. That year, he topped 100 pitches in 18 of his starts, including a 130-pitch game May 28 against the Dodgers. He was 0-1 in two starts against the Mets last season.

home_pitcher_note: Uncharacteristically throwing his offspeed pitches for strikes, Perez flashed a sharp slider and some stellar control on Friday in St. Louis. That not only helped him negate his dip in fastball velocity, but also allowed him to submit one of his finest efforts of the past two seasons. Whether Perez can sustain his low-velocity success remains to be seen. But if he can continue to feature the type of control he had against the Cardinals, Perez should, at the very least, be serviceable. His next test will come against the Dodgers, who walked seven times but could not beat him last July at Citi Field.
away_pitcher_note: Silva is coming off his second straight stellar start to kick off the season, having allowed five hits while striking out five and walking none in seven solid innings during a 7-2 win over the Astros in his first Cubs start at Wrigley Field. Silva last pitched against the Mets on June 18, 2007, when he gave up 10 hits and four runs in six innings in a losing effort as a member of the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Santana defeated the Cubs in his only start against them as a member of the Mets, at Shea Stadium on Sept. 28, 2008. He allowed two runs in eight innings. His career record against them, including four starts with the Twins, is 2-0. Alfonso Soriano is the only Cubs player with more than six career at-bats against Santana, and he is hitless in 10. Santana has produced a 9-4 record and 2.68 ERA in 16 starts at Citi Field. His best performance in three starts this season came Saturday in St. Louis in the 20-inning game. He threw seven scoreless innings, allowing four hits and a walk and striking out nine.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny took the loss in his second start of the season, against the Astros on Saturday. The left-hander gave up two runs on three hits in three innings, but he left the game for precautionary reasons after getting hit by line drive on his throwing shoulder. Gorzelanny last stared against the Mets on April 30, 2008, and got the win, pitching five shutout, one-hit innings for the Pirates. It may be Gorzelanny's final chance to prove he deserves to stay in the starting rotation with Ted Lilly scheduled to come off the 15-day disabled list and rejoin the starting staff.

home_pitcher_note: Maine produced a no-decision in his only home start this season. In 34 starts at Shea Stadium and Citi Field in the previous three seasons, he won 17 of 26 decisions and produced a 3.56 ERA. His 38 road starts in the same period produced a 15-15 record and 4.62 ERA, and he has been ineffective in two road starts this season -- 0-1 record, 12.38 ERA and 20 baserunners in eight innings. His renewed emphasis on his fastball served him well for four innings in his most recent start, against the Cardinals Sunday, but the fourth home run against him in 14 innings essentially ended his workday. Alfonso Soriano has two home runs but no other hits in 17 career at-bats against Maine.
away_pitcher_note: Kawakami proved to be effective while utilizing his sinker against the Giants during his season debut. But while opposing the more patient Rockies lineup on Saturday, he left too many pitches up in the zone and fell behind in the count too often.  The Japanese right-hander allowed four runs on eight hits in five innings against the Rockies.  He needed 103 pitches to complete the outing and just 65 pitches to complete the six-inning effort against the Giants. In five appearances (three starts) against the Mets last year, Kawakami went 1-2 with a 2.19 ERA.   His finest effort against them occurred on Aug. 20, when he limited them to one run and seven hits in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Niese's three starts have produced results that were respectively good, bad and indifferent. The best came most recently, Monday against the Cubs at Citi Field. It produced a no-decision though he threw five shutout innings and wasn't charged with a run until after he had been removed with two out in the sixth. The run was unearned. He struck out seven, equaling his career high. Niese has surrendered one home run in 16 2/3 innings, and that was on the road. But he is allowing more hits, 25, than he'd like. Left-handed hitters have a .364 slugging percentage in 11 at-bats against him, hardly an ample sample. Right-handed hitters' slugging percentage is .516 in 62 at-bats. He has two career starts against the Braves. One was a victory, the other a no-decision. His ERA in 12 2/3 innings against them is 3.55.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens quieted some concerns about his right shoulder on Sunday afternoon when he regained his velocity and limited the Rockies to three runs in a season-high eight innings. Just five days earlier in San Diego, he was displaying a fastball that rested between 87-89 mph and allowing a career-high eight runs in just 3 1/3 innings. His rebound effort against the Rockies was marred by solo shots in the seventh and eighth innings. But for the most part, the 24-year-old right-hander had the successful form that enabled him to allow two earned runs or fewer in 26 of his 34 starts last year. Jurrjens went 4-0 with a 1.60 ERA in his five starts against the Mets last year.

home_pitcher_note: After Pelfrey defeated the Cubs Tuesday, the Mets had won six games, and he was responsible for half the victories and the team's lone save. Pelfrey, who has pitched at least six innings in eight straight starts, hasn't allowed a run in 19 innings, equaling his longest career shutout streak. Against the listless Cubs, he surrendered merely three hits, none in the first four innings, and walked three, none in the last four. His improving cutter produced four of his six strikeouts.  He also became the first pitcher to win two starts with a save in between in a five-day period since 1988 when John Candelaria achieved that arcane feat for the Yankees. He has a 2-5 record and a 6.09 ERA in nine starts and one relief appearance against the Braves. Brian McCann has a .444 average and one home run in 27 career at-bats against Pelfrey. Chipper Jones has eight walks, two home runs, four other hits and a .333 average in 26 plate appearances against the Mets starter.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson left Tuesday night's 102-pitch effort against the Phillies frustrated by the belief that he was either tipping his pitches or proving to be too predictable. The 23-year-old right-hander allowed two earned runs in just 4 2/3 innings and one of the primary reasons he compiled a high early pitch count came via the 23 pitches the Phillies fouled. Hanson's command hasn't been as sharp as it was last year, but he still hasn't allowed more than two earned runs in any of his first three outings. During his only previous start against the Mets last year, Hanson allowed just three hits in seven scoreless innings.
summary: 2010-04-25 - Atlanta Braves @ New York Mets (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: The Perez Pendulum continues to swing. Perez's last start wasn't on either ended of the swing. He lost to the offensively-challenged Cubs, allowing 11 baserunners in five innings, including seven in an 11-batter sequence in the his final two innings, but he allowed merely three runs. He didn't break, but he did bend considerably. Now he faces an opponent he has beaten three times in four starts in the last three seasons. Moreover, Perez has a 2.84 ERA in 25 1/3 innings in those starts. His success may be in some jeopardy Monday. Russell Martin, Matt Kemp, Garrett Anderson and Jamey Carroll have batted .486 in 35 composite at-bats against him.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda wasn't too pleased with his outing on Wednesday except for the fact that the Dodgers won, largely due to a 14-run, 18-hit outburst against the Reds at Great American Ball Park. Kuroda kept the game close, giving the Dodgers a chance to rally from an early 3-1 deficit. He allowed six runs, three earned, on seven hits, struck out four and walked two in a 103-pitch effort. He allowed two home runs. Prior to Wednesday's outing, Kuroda had gone 15 innings without allowing a home run and had issued just two walks in 14 innings. Dodgers manager Joe Torre wasn't concerned with Kuroda's outing and was impressed with the way he battled for a victory despite not having his best stuff.
summary: 2010-04-26 - Los Angeles Dodgers @ New York Mets (Postponed)

home_pitcher_note: Santana has allowed one run in 13 1/3 innings over his past two starts, and he's off to an exceptional start, walking only six and striking out 22 in his first 24 1/3 innings. Santana is 2-0 with a 0.61 ERA in two career starts against the Dodgers.

away_pitcher_note: Vicente Padilla was scheduled for this start until going on the disabled list. Haeger will make this start with three days' rest, which is less of an issue with a knuckleball pitcher. By doing that, the club can keep Jon Link an extra day for bullpen use. Haeger is coming off an improved start in Washington, but a loss nonetheless. He did take the game into the sixth inning and kept his club in it. He allowed two homers to Adam Dunn, a solo shot on a knuckleball that didn't knuckle, and a two-run shot on a fastball down the middle. He walked only one, the last batter he faced.
summary: 2010-04-27 - Los Angeles Dodgers (5) @ New York Mets (10) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Maine was removed from his most recent start, Friday against the Braves, in the fourth inning because of muscle spasms and pain in his left -- yes, left -- elbow. He threw 63 pitches in 3 2/3 innings, allowing four hits and two walks and striking out three. Now he is to pitch against an opponent that has been a problem for him. Maine has a 1-4 record in six career starts against the Dodgers. Beware Ronnie Belliard, who has a .600 average and one home run in 15 career at-bats against Maine, and Rafael Furcal, who has batted .545 in 11 at-bats against him. The Mets have lost five of Maine's eight most recent starts over two seasons.
away_pitcher_note: Ely's name dropped out of the probable pitchers list for the Triple-A Albuquerque Dukes and showed up in the Dodgers clubhouse Tuesday, although the club has not confirmed he will make this start. The Dodgers need a pitcher Wednesday to take the place of disabled Opening Day starter Vicente Padilla, and Ely -- a 23-year-old right-hander taken out of Miami (Ohio) University in the third round of the 2007 Draft -- could be it. He went 14-2 with a 2.82 ERA at Double-A last year and is 2-1 with a 3.00 ERA in three starts for Albuquerque, having last pitched April 21. He has 12 strikeouts, but also eight walks, in 18 innings.
summary: 2010-04-28 - Los Angeles Dodgers (3) @ New York Mets (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Just when it looked like Kyle Kendrick had taken a step forward, he took a step backward Sunday in a start against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field. He threw eight scoreless innings against the Atlanta Braves on April 20 and had thrown four more scoreless innings against Arizona before he allowed five runs in the fifth inning in an 8-6 loss. Kendrick is going to have to start pitching better with right-hander Joe Blanton and closer Brad Lidge expected to rejoin the team soon.
away_pitcher_note: After four starts, Niese still is seeking his first extended and successful start, not to mention his first victory. His next chance comes on Friday night against a team he never has faced. Because of the Mets' off-day Thursday, Niese will have abnormal rest -- five days -- before he opposes Chase Utley, Ryan Howard, et al. Extra rest is not a bad thing to have when pitching in that adversarial arena. Niese has allowed one home run in 22 innings, that to Ryan Spilborghs in Denver, and four in 61 2/3 innings in his career. But CBP can change a pitcher's ERA and home run total quickly. Niese has been more effective against left-handed hitters than right-handed thus far this season, and that constitutes a change from his two previous -- and abbreviated -- big league tours. He does appear more inclined to pitching inside to them, and his cutter now gives him a weapon for right-handed hitters.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay proved he is human on Monday in a loss to the San Francisco Giants at AT&T Park. He allowed 10 hits and five runs in seven innings to pick up his first loss of the season. Halladay wasn't as sharp as he had been in his previous four starts, but the Giants also hit some pretty good pitches. This will be Halladay's first taste of the Phillies-Mets rivalry, and the slumping Phillies will be counting on him to throw well.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey hasn't allowed a run in 24 innings. How he extended his streak from 19 to 24 was attributable to his increased repertoire. With his fastball and newly-minted cutter failing him Sunday night, he threw a variety of pitches to keep the Braves off-balance and emerged with another victory. He surrendered five hits and five walks and struck out three in five innings, throwing 61 pitches in the first two innings and 106 over all. He has been moderately successful against the Phillies in the last three years -- a 4-2 record and 4.82 ERA in nine starts. But his appearances in Citizens Bank Park haven't been too rewarding -- 1-1 record and 7.17 ERA in four starts. Pelfrey, who has allowed no home runs in 26 innings this season, has allowed merely 37 in his 505 career innings -- 10 at Shea Stadium, six at Citi Field and six at Citizens Bank. Chase Utley has hit four against him, at least one at each site.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer pitched well enough to win Tuesday in a loss to the San Francisco Giants at AT&T Park. He allowed 10 hits and four runs in six innings, which is good enough for the Phillies offense on most nights. But the Phillies have been struggling offensively and provided Moyer no support. Moyer will have to be much better Sunday against the Mets. He is facing Mets ace Johan Santana, so runs figure to be even more scarce.
away_pitcher_note: On a chilly day in the Windy Citi, Santana persevered through 115 pitches, a season high for him, and shut down the Dodgers for six innings Tuesday. His work led to a shutout victory and set him up to face the Phillies in their small ballpark. The Mets usually opt to have Santana get as much rest as possible, and with an off-day two days after his start against the Dodgers, they could have afforded him five days' rest. But he would have missed the Phillies that way. And, worse, the Mets would have Ollie Perez pitching Sunday. This way, their Sunday night starter will be one who has a 4-1 career and 2.98 ERA in eight starts against the Phillies in the last three years and a 1-1 record and 3.21 ERA in four starts at CBP in the same span. Ryan Howard and Chase Utley have hit three home runs each against Santana. And Raul Ibanez is batting .350 in 40 career at-bats against the Mets starter.

home_pitcher_note: In his third straight seven-inning start, the rookie Leake gave up one earned run on five hits with two walks and five strikeouts for a 6-4 victory over the Astros. Through his first four innings, he surrendered only one first-inning hit and faced the minimum 12 batters. He also used his sinker to induce a pair of Carlos Lee double plays. "He can throw strikes and get ahead of hitters. As long as he does that, he's going to be fine," Reds catcher Ramon Hernandez said.
away_pitcher_note: Perez, who will start with five days of rest, is barely averaging five innings per outing, having thrown 20 2/3 innings in four starts. He didn't make it through four innings against the Dodgers last time out, as he removed after walking four and allowing three runs in 3 2/3 innings. Perez is 9-5 with a 4.54 ERA in his career against Cincinnati.

home_pitcher_note: In a 4-2 win over the Astros on Thursday, Arroyo pitched 6 2/3 innings, but he began with six scoreless until his first run crossed on Hunter Pence's leadoff homer in the seventh. Overall, Arroyo gave up two runs and six hits with three walks and seven strikeouts for his first victory of 2010.  Said Arroyo: "I had probably the best I've had all year. I had a little bit more on the fastball, which I was looking for a while. I had good command of my other pitches."
away_pitcher_note: Throwing, by his estimation, over 80 percent fastballs, Maine featured late life on his heater and had some renewed success on the mound last Wednesday. The result was Maine's first victory of the season, in which he struck out nine Dodgers in six-plus innings. Eventually, he plans on working more breaking balls back into his game plan -- but not to the same extent as before. For now, he will continue to challenge hitters with his fastball, which will only work at the Great American Ball Park if he keeps them down in the zone. Maine has allowed three home runs in nine career innings at the park, producing an 0-2 record and an 11.00 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: One of Cueto's better outings of the season was cut short by thunderstorms, but he still earned the victory over the Cardinals, 3-2, on Friday. Cueto pitched five innings and allowed two earned runs -- on Matt Holliday's bases-loaded single in the third -- and five hits with one intentional walk and three strikeouts.  He threw a total of 82 pitches in the game, but a two-hour, 32-minute rain delay prevented him from continuing.
away_pitcher_note: Niese exploited the Phillies' weakness -- a 2010 development -- to gain his first victory on Friday night at Citizens Bank Park. He allowed four hits and one walk and struck out seven in seven innings while the Mets provided substantial support. Now, he faces Jay Bruce and Joey Votto, both left-handed hitters. The league's left-handed swingers have batted merely .190 against Niese thus far, albeit in 21 at-bats. Niese never has faced the Reds, but he spent his childhood no more than 2 1/2 hours away from Cincinnati. No one can accurately predict the effect of pitching before family and friends.

home_pitcher_note: The perfect record and streak of scoreless innings are gone, obliterated by the Phillies' onslaught on Saturday in Philadelphia. Pelfrey now faces a challenge as great as Chase Utley, Ryan Howard, Jayson Werth and Shane Victorino -- getting back on the bike. Given the resolve he demonstrated through 27 innings of threats and zeroes, no one anticipates Pelfrey taking a giant step in the wrong direction because of a six-run one-inning blemish. When he opposes the Giants on Friday night, he will have had five days' rest, one more than normal, after a grueling 82-pitch start. He has pitched effectively in three career outings against the Giants, producing a 1-1 record and a 1.77 ERA. They have batted merely .187 in 20 1/3 innings against him. Pelfrey's ERA is 1.00 in three night starts and in three starts at Citi Field, where he's 3-0 this season. Left-handed hitters have a .292 slugging percentage in 48 at-bats against him this season. No Giants have more than six at-bats against Pelfrey.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez has struggled in his career against Colorado, and Sunday was no different. Sanchez, who came into the game 2-3 with a 6.85 ERA in 15 career appearances against the Rockies, allowed three runs in 4 2/3 innings to take the loss, raising his ERA to 2.48. Sanchez still has a strikeout-to-walk ratio of 37-28, but did walk five batters in each of his past two outings. In April, he recorded back-to-back double-digit strikeout games for the first time in his career -- April 14 against Pittsburgh and April 20 against San Diego. In four career starts against the Mets, the left-hander is 2-1 with 13 walks, 26 strikeouts and a 3.91 ERA. New York has a .234 batting average against him in that span. He has made one start at Citi Field, in which he allowed two runs and four hits in seven innings but did not get a decision.
summary: 2010-05-07 - San Francisco Giants (4) @ New York Mets (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The worst start of Johan Santana's career came last Sunday night at Citizens Bank Park, where he served up four home runs and 10 total runs against the Phillies. Citing a lack of fastball command, Santana walked 47-year-old pitcher Jamie Moyer with the bases loaded, then allowed a grand slam to Shane Victorino. He would prefer to forget all that on Saturday against the Giants, a team that has never beaten him in five career meetings. Last year, Santana went 1-0 with a 5.27 ERA in two starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer comes into this game against the Mets with an undesirable record and ERA. However, he has come on strong of late. Wellemeyer shined in his last start, which resulted in a 6-2 victory over Philadelphia on April 27. Wellemeyer went seven innings in the game, allowing two runs on three hits. Then, on Sunday against Colorado, he came in to relieve Jonathan Sanchez and pitched three scoreless innings. In four starts against New York, he has an 0-2 record, and the Mets have a .363 batting average against him. His ERA vs. New York is 6.67, and he has totaled 15 walks and 14 strikeouts. In one start at Citi Field, he is 0-1, having allowed five runs in 7 2/3 innings.
summary: 2010-05-08 - San Francisco Giants (4) @ New York Mets (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Neither Good Ollie nor Bad Ollie showed up on Monday in Cincinnati. Instead, some hybrid of the two walked four Reds batters but held them to two runs over six innings -- no small feat for a fly-ball pitcher at the Great American Ball Park. It was his second quality start in five tries this season. Perez has not faced his next opponent, the Giants, since June 2008, when he allowed five hits, two walks and six runs in 1/3 of an inning at AT&T Park. And the Giants are an improved offensive club since then.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum fanned 13 Marlins batters on Tuesday and finally got the run support he'd been asking for, but unfortunately he allowed a three-run homer to Hanley Ramirez in the sixth inning. Dan Uggla later hit another three-run homer off reliever Sergio Romo to ensure another no-decision for the two-time Cy Young Award winner. Lincecum's final line: seven innings, five hits, three runs, one walk and 13 strikeouts. Take away the one mistake to Ramirez and it's another typical dominant Lincecum outing. In three career starts against the Mets, Lincecum is 0-1 with a 5.68 ERA. This will be his first start at Citi Field.
summary: 2010-05-09 - San Francisco Giants (6) @ New York Mets (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Though Maine continued to deal in the high 80s with his fastball last Tuesday in Cincinnati, he featured more late movement on the pitch than he has all season. That allowed him to torment lefties Joey Votto and Jay Bruce, generating swings and misses rather than hits. It's not yet perfect for Maine, but, in his words, its getting there. Over his last three starts (one of them shortened by injury), Maine is 1-0 with a 2.30 ERA. And that, certainly, qualifies as progress. He will look to continue the trend at home against the Nationals, the only team he beat twice last season.
away_pitcher_note: Atilano started Wednesday and had his worst outing of his young career. It was a game in which Atilano had a tough time finding the strike zone. He walked five hitters and gave up six runs in 5 1/3 innings. He was pitching on seven days' rest, but he didn't use that as an excuse for his disappointing outing. Instead, Atilano said he was too pumped up to face the Braves, the team that traded him to Washington on Aug. 31, 2006. The trade occurred while Atilano was still recovering from Tommy John surgery.

home_pitcher_note: Though Niese served up 12 hits in six innings to the Reds last Wednesday in Cincinnati, he walked none and allowed only four of those runners to score. It was enough for a no-decision and nothing more, but that was hardly a step back for a rookie who has been one of the Mets' most consistent pitchers this season. Niese is the only Mets starter to last at least five innings in all six of his outings. His next start will come against the Nationals, the lone divisional opponent he has never faced.
away_pitcher_note: Right-hander Livan Hernandez's re-emergence as a rotation stalwart has obscured an equally impressive comeback by Olsen, who was non-tendered in December, re-signed a day later, struggled with his velocity in Spring Training and started the season in the minors. Since being recalled from Triple-A Syracuse to start on April 15, the lanky lefty's stuff has gotten progressively better. In his last start on Thursday, Olsen took a no-hitter into the eighth inning against the Braves until his scoreless streak of 20 1/3 innings ended on a night when he allowed two runs on two hits in 7 1-3 innings. The fastball is back into the low 90s with movement and Olsen is using a tricky slider as an effective out pitch.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey logged his longest start of the season against the Giants on Friday, pitching 7 1/3 innings while giving up eight hits and three earned runs. The big right-hander threw just 85 pitches against San Francisco, 61 of them strikes, surrendering no walks and striking out four batters. Pelfrey faced the Nationals in his first outing of the season, allowing two runs in six innings in a win. For his career, Pelfrey is 4-5 with a 3.86 ERA against Washington.
away_pitcher_note: On May 1, Stammen lasted four innings and gave up three earned runs on seven hits against the Marlins. On Friday, he faced the Marlins again and was much better, lasting 6 1/3 innings, while allowing an earned run on four hits. He struck out a career-high eight batters and walked none. At one point during the game, he retired 14 straight batters.

home_pitcher_note: The Marlins return home from a six-game road trip with Johnson on the mound. The 26-year-old right-hander lost to New York on Opening Day, as he gave up four runs in five innings, with four walks. But for his career, he is 7-1 with a 2.69 ERA lifetime in 10 starts. In his last start, JJ gave up three runs in six innings at Washington, striking out five. Johnson was in line for the win but settled for a no decision.
away_pitcher_note: Santana bounced back from the worst outing of his career (3 2/3 innings pitched, 10 runs against the Phillies) with a solid performance against the Giants. The lefty allowed four runs over 7 2/3 innings in a no decision. Next up are the Marlins, who Santana faced and earned a win against in his first start of the season, allowing one run over six innings while striking out five batters. Santana is 6-1 with a 1.66 ERA against Florida for his career, his lowest ERA against any team he has registered at least five starts against.

home_pitcher_note: Control was a problem for Sanchez in his last start, a no-decision at Washington. The right-hander matched his season high with four walks, and he threw a wild pitch. Two of the runners scored. The 4 2/3-inning stint was Sanchez's shortest of the season. In each of his first five starts, he tossed at least six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Against the Giants on Sunday, Perez failed to make it out of the fourth inning for the second time in his last three starts. The lefty has really struggled with his control, walking 15 over that span, including seven in his no-decision against San Francisco. He has now walked more hitters (25) than he has struck out (22) in six starts this season. Perez will face the Marlins for the first time since 2008, when he went 3-0 with a 2.23 ERA in six starts against Florida.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander comes off arguably his finest outing of the season. In six innings against the Cubs, he gave up two runs on seven hits. The win was his first since beating the Phillies on April 18. In his first two May starts, he is 1-1 with a 3.18 ERA, striking out eight in 11 1/3 innings. On April 8 at New York, he threw five innings and beat the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Maine continues to rebound from his poor start to the season, logging his third consecutive quality start against the Nationals on Monday. The righty went six innings, allowed three runs and struck out five, which earned him a loss in the 3-2 game. Maine faced the Marlins in New York in the first series of the season, lasting five innings and surrendering four runs in a no-decision. Last year, Maine logged more starts against Florida than any other team, going 2-1 with a 3.74 ERA in four games.

home_pitcher_note: Now with 43 career wins, Nolasco has moved ahead of Ryan Dempster (42) into fourth place all-time in Marlins victories. Nolasco comes off a win at Chicago, where he gave up one run in seven innings. For the season, the right-hander has 35 strikeouts in 46 2/3 innings. Nolasco beat the Mets on April 7 at New York, giving up three runs in 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Niese's first career start against the Nationals was one to forget. The lefty escaped with a no-decision after surrendering six runs on six hits and five walks in 4 1/3 innings. Niese struggled with his control all game and never fully recovered from a first-inning three-run homer by Adam Dunn. Niese will face the only team to hand him a loss this year when he pitches the final game of the series in Miami. He logged a quality start against the Marlins in his first outing of the season, allowing three runs over six innings, but the Mets' offense only scratched out one run.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe produced one of his finest starts of the season on Wednesday, when he limited the Brewers to two runs in six innings. It marked the first time that he has completed six innings since April 10. The veteran sinkerballer has gone 2-3 with a 6.41 ERA in his past five starts. Opponents have hit .309 and reached base at a .358 clip against him during this span. Lowe went 2-1 with a 6.94 ERA in five starts against the Mets last year. This ERA was damaged on Aug. 18, when he allowed them eight earned runs in just 3 2/3 innings. He surrendered three earned runs or fewer in each of the other four outings against them.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey did not reach the sixth inning for the third time in his last four starts Wednesday against the Nationals. He struck out the side in order in the first inning, but never looked comfortable on the mound after that, settling for his second consecutive no-decision. The Braves are next on the schedule for Big Pelf, a team he beat on April 25, 1-0. Pelfrey didn't allow a run against Atlanta, but five walks accelerated his pitch count and he was out of the game after the fifth inning. He is 3-5 with a 5.58 ERA for his career against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Medlen will be making his second start of the season in place of the injured Jair Jurrjens.  During his first start, the versatile right-hander limited the Phillies to one run and nine hits in 4 1/3 innings. He managed to throw 88 pitches, despite the fact that he hadn't thrown more than 44 in any of his previous 12 relief appearances this year. Medlen has shown good control while recording 19 strikeouts and issuing three walks in 22 innings. This will be his first career start against the Mets. In four career relief appearances against them, he has worked 6 1/3 scoreless innings and surrendered six hits.
away_pitcher_note: Featuring one of his better changeups of the season, Santana held the Marlins to one unearned run last Wednesday in Miami, allowing six hits and striking out five. But Marlins starter Josh Johnson matched him pitch for pitch, preventing Santana from earning a decision. He will look to earn his first victory in four starts this Tuesday in Atlanta, a place that has treated him kindly over the years. In three career starts at Turner Field, Santana has a 1.71 ERA. He was 1-2 with a 1.33 ERA overall against the Braves last season.

home_pitcher_note: The Nationals have decided that right-hander Livan Hernandez will pitch on three days' rest against the Mets on Wednesday night at Nationals Park. The Nationals were thinking about calling up a Minor Leaguer for that game, but after throwing 100 pitches in the first game of a day-night doubleheader against the Rockies, Hernandez went to manager Jim Riggleman's office and volunteered to take the ball. Washington needed a pitcher Wednesday because the day-night doubleheader messed up their rotation plans. Hernandez was originally scheduled to start Friday against the Rockies, but the game was postponed because of rain, and he had to pitch Saturday instead.
away_pitcher_note: Though the Mets have not yet announced who will step into the rotation in place of Oliver Perez, all signs point to the knuckleballer Dickey. In eight starts for Triple-A Buffalo, Dickey was 4-2 with a 2.33 ERA, numbers made better by a complete game one-hitter in late April. In his most recent start, Dickey fired eight innings of three-run ball in a victory. He will be making his first start since last August, and has not faced the Nationals since being blown out by them in June 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Atilano started for Washington on Saturday, and Colorado played long ball with him in the third inning. Carlos Gonzalez hit a two-run homer on a curveball. Atilano said he should have thrown a changeup instead. Smith followed Gonzalez with a homer to give the Rockies a 3-0 lead. Atilano lasted five innings and allowed three runs on four hits. He threw 93 pitches, 59 for strikes. Atilano didn't like that he was often behind in the count.
away_pitcher_note: Twelve straight balls to open the game doomed Maine last Saturday in Miami, resulting in a 7-2 loss to the Marlins. Though Maine featured what he, pitching coach Dan Warthen and catcher Rod Barajas all considered some of his best stuff in the season warming up before the game, it did not translate onto the mound. As a result, Maine dropped his second straight decision. The first of those came against the Nationals, though Maine did not pitch particularly poorly in that one. He will look to rebound against the Nats in Washington, a city that has not been particularly kind to him over the years. Maine holds a 7.00 career ERA at Nationals Park, after posting a 5.56 lifetime mark at old RFK.

home_pitcher_note: In lieu of Jon Niese, who aggravated his right hamstring last Sunday in Miami, Takahashi will make the first big league start of his career. Predominantly a starting pitcher over nine seasons in Japan, Takahashi was 3-1 with a 3.12 ERA in 15 appearances out of the bullpen for the Mets, four of them lasting at least three innings. Still, Takahashi is not stretched out as a starter and will be limited to roughly 85 pitches Friday night at Citi Field. In his first big league season, he has not yet faced the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez gets the nod as the Yankees begin Interleague play against the Mets at Citi Field. Vazquez's last start was on May 12 at Detroit, where he hurled seven innings of two-run, five-hit ball with two walks and seven strikeouts in a losing effort as the Yankees were shut out, 2-0. But Vazquez made his third career relief appearance on May 17 against the Red Sox, striking out the only batter he faced to record the win in New York's 11-9 victory. Vazquez is 9-8 with a 3.37 ERA in 23 starts against the Mets lifetime, and was 1-1 with a 4.61 ERA in two starts against them last season.
summary: 2010-05-21 - New York Yankees (2) @ New York Mets (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: With the rotation falling apart around him, Pelfrey gave the Mets exactly what they needed last Monday in Atlanta: a stellar start. Inducing three double plays, Pelfrey limited the Braves to two runs over 7 2/3 innings, striking out three and walking two. His next start will come against the Yankees, a team that beat him despite a relatively strong -- albeit brief, just five innings -- start last year at Citi Field. In two career starts against the Yankees, Pelfrey is 1-1 with a 5.40 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Hughes labored through his worst outing of the season last Monday, handing back nearly all of a five-run first-inning cushion in the Yankees' 11-9 win over the Red Sox. Hughes survived only five innings -- his shortest outing since his first start of the season -- and surrendered a season-high five runs. That's only one run fewer than he allowed in his first half-dozen starts combined. Hughes struggled mainly to put hitters away, with his pitch count inflated by long at-bats and myriad foul balls. Hughes has faced the Mets twice before in relief, tossing a total of 2 1/3 scoreless innings. Current Mets are just 2-for-14 off Hughes collectively.
summary: 2010-05-22 - New York Yankees (3) @ New York Mets (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: For a third straight outing, Santana pitched well but came away with a no-decision. This time, a two-run home run by Troy Glaus in the third inning doomed him, though they were the only runs the Braves could muster off Santana in seven innings last Tuesday at Turner Field. Santana next faces the Yankees, who thumped him for nine runs in three innings last year in the Bronx. He will expect something better on Sunday night at Citi Field -- and for good reason. Santana is 4-2 with a 4.40 ERA in 11 career games against the Yankees. And he is 3-1 with a 3.19 ERA this year at Citi Field.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia gets to sharpen his stuff against a National League lineup, as the ace gets the ball in the Subway Series finale. Sabathia took a no-decision on May 18 after the bullpen blew his seven innings of one-run, four-hit ball against the Red Sox in a 7-6 loss. He hasn't logged a victory since May 3, which was against the Orioles. Sabathia is 2-0 with a 1.20 ERA in two career starts against the Mets, including a win on June 26 at Citi Field last season.
summary: 2010-05-23 - New York Yankees (4) @ New York Mets (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: After flirting with the idea of using Raul Valdes against the Phillies, Mets manager Jerry Manuel ultimately decided on Dickey. Dickey will be the second consecutive knuckleballer to face the Phillies, as Boston's Tim Wakefield threw eight shutout innings against Philadelphia on Sunday. The Mets' soft tosser will be making his second start of the season. Dickey logged six innings and two earned runs in a no decision against Washington. This will be Dickey's first career starts against the Phillies and first career start in Citi Field.
away_pitcher_note: Nobody really knew what to expect from Jamie Moyer this season. He struggled last season and spent time in the hospital in the offseason recovering from a couple surgeries. But Moyer, 47, has pitched well. He is 5-3 with a 4.20 ERA through eight starts. He is 2-1 with a 2.42 ERA in his past three starts, and 4-2 with a 3.35 ERA in his past six. He has pitched at least six innings in each start this season, which has been huge for the rotation and the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: Making his Major League starting debut against one of the game's most potent offenses, Takahashi blanked the Yankees over six innings on Friday at Citi Field. Limited to a relatively strict pitch count, Takahashi went beyond that, throwing 101 pitches, allowing five hits and one walk and striking out five in what manager Jerry Manuel called an audition for future starts. Needless to say, Takahashi passed, and will take the mound Wednesday against the Phillies. He has faced them once before, allowing one run in 1 1/3 innings of relief earlier this month in Philadelphia.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton pitched well in his first three starts this season, but he didn't have the numbers to prove it. He finally got some of those numbers last week in a 5-4 victory over the Chicago Cubs at Citizens Bank Park. He allowed five hits and three runs in seven innings, which added to the recent string of strong pitching performances from the Phillies rotation. If Blanton can pick up where he left off last week, it will solidify a rotation that has been one of the best in baseball in May.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey dropped his ERA below 3.00 by allowing just one run in six innings against the Yankees on Saturday. Mets manager Jerry Manuel said he will be counting on him and Johan Santana for consistent results with the rotation currently in flux. The Phillies, however, roughed up both of those starters when the teams last met. Pelfrey was tagged for six runs in four innings and came away with his only loss of the season. He is 4-3 against Philadelphia for his career, but his ERA is 5.43.
away_pitcher_note: It looks like Hamels is finally putting everything together. He allowed just three hits, one run and one walk and struck out eight in seven innings Friday in a 5-2 victory over the Boston Red Sox at Citizens Bank Park. Hamels' ERA has not been under 4.00 this late in the season since 2008. He is 3-0 with a 2.36 ERA in four starts this month, compared to a 2-2 mark and a 5.28 ERA in April. The Phillies had high hopes for Roy Halladay and Hamels atop the Phillies' rotation in 2010. They think they've seen flashes of what they'd hoped for already this month.

home_pitcher_note: After a rough first inning in which he allowed four runs after recording just two outs, Gallardo did not allow a run while surrendering just two hits over his last five innings at Target Field. For the third straight start, however, Gallardo settled for a no-decision, as the Brewers offense was quiet until the ninth in the club's 12-inning loss to the Twins. The outing also broke a streak of five straight quality starts for Gallardo. He'll look to get back on track Friday against the New York Mets, as he hopes to record his first win since May 7th in Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Santana continues to pitch deep into games for the Mets. The lefty went 7 2/3 innings in a 6-4 win against the Yankees on Sunday, marking the fourth consecutive start he has gone at least seven innings. He has also allowed only three earned runs in his last three outings combined. All of Santana's wins have come at home this season, and he will be looking to register his first road win in Milwaukee. In four starts away from Citi Field, his road ERA (4.38) is more than a full run higher than his home ERA (3.19).

home_pitcher_note: Though he hasn't started a game since his first start of the season on May 18 in Cincinnati, Parra picked up his first win of the season in the series finale against the Twins as the Brewers avoided the sweep. Parra also picked up a loss the night before, as he was called on to pitch in the 11th inning with the Brewers out of other options. He was scratched from his scheduled start the next day as a result but came on to pitch the fourth and the fifth, in which he did not allow a run, yielding three hits while striking out two and walking a pair.
away_pitcher_note: With the Mets needing a spot start before Jonathon Niese or John Maine is healthy enough to return to the rotation, manager Jerry Manuel said that Nieve, who made seven starts for the Mets last season, is the leading candidate to get the nod Saturday against the Brewers. Nieve has made 18 starts in his career with the Mets and Astros, going 5-6 with 4.11 ERA. Nieve worked a hitless ninth inning in Wednesday's night game to keep him sharp for his start.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf wasn't happy in his two starts before Tuesday's win over the Astros, calling his May 14 loss to the Phillies "embarrassing," and saying after his May 19 outing in Pittsburgh, "I'm concerned that I stink." His performance against the struggling Astros, though, left him smiling. Wolf allowed no runs on four hits in seven strong innings for his first win at Miller Park since his April 6 Brewers debut. He snapped a streak of 20 straight games that a Brewers starter pitched fewer than seven innings, since Yovani Gallardo went seven in a 2-1 win at San Diego on May 1. "We need to do that more," Wolf said.
away_pitcher_note: Dickey worked his way through two bases-loaded jams in the first three innings and a line drive to his left elbow to earn the victory in his last start against the Phillies. The knuckleballer blanked Philadelphia in six innings Tuesday before eventually coming out of the game when his left elbow started swelling. Dickey has been cleared to play medically and is expected to get the start Sunday in Milwaukee. He attributes his recent success to trusting his knuckleball more as he has felt more comfortable throwing it from behind in the count. This has allowed his fastball to become more of a weapon, surprising hitters who are getting approximately 80 percent knuckleballs.

home_pitcher_note: Correia had a no-decision in his last start against the Cardinals, nearly matching St. Louis starter Jaime Garcia, as he tossed six shutout innings of his own. Correia, who hasn't won since April 28, allowed five hits but had six walks to go with five strikeouts. "His timing has been off his last few starts with his delivery," Padres manager Bud Black said of the walks. For someone who received plenty of run support early this season -- the Padres scored 17 runs, five, 10 and six runs in the span of four starts in April -- Correia has now been backed by two, one, one and now zero runs in his past four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Takahashi hasn't allowed a run in his two starts since moving into the rotation. He posted back-to-back six-inning shutout performances against the Yankees and Phillies during the last homestand. The 35-year-old rookie from Japan doesn't throw hard, but his array of offspeed pitches has been very effective during his brief time in the Majors. The lefty has struck out 44 batters in 38 innings so far this season. He's also done a good job of keeping hitters in the park, allowing only one home run.

away_pitcher_note: Once again, Dickey ran into trouble early in his last start against the Marlins, but settled into another solid outing. home_pitcher_note: After a couple of rocky outings, Matusz has strung together two straight good games for the Orioles. away_pitcher_note: After promptly submitting two stellar starts upon joining the rotation, Takahashi has now endured two consecutive poor ones. home_pitcher_note: After getting off to a solid start to the season but being plagued by poor run support, Millwood has regressed in his last three starts. away_pitcher_note: To throw nine innings of one-run ball last Tuesday against the Padres, Pelfrey needed merely 103 pitches. He struck out six and induced 17 groundouts and threw 110 pitches.

away_pitcher_note: Knuckleball specialist R.A. Dickey has been a real find for the Mets and will attempt to continue his magical run against the Indians, against whom he owns a 1-0 lifetime record in eight appearances, including two starts. Dickey has been using an effective power knuckler, which flutters to the plate as high as 82 mph. Hitters claim the increased speed -- about 15-20 mph faster than the typical knuckleball -- and its movement make it a difficult pitch to hit. For now, Mets skipper Jerry Manuel is confident enough with Dickey in the rotation that he's backed off on pleas for general manager Omar Minaya to add an experienced starter to the rotation.

away_pitcher_note: In danger of losing his rotation spot once John Maine returns from the disabled list, Takahashi enjoyed his first solid outing in three starts last weekend in Baltimore. Not only will Takahashi have to face the mighty Yankees, but he must do so having faced them just four weeks earlier. That may make things difficult for the 35-year-old rookie, who relies on deception.
summary: 2010-06-18 - New York Mets (4) @ New York Yankees (0) (Final)

To make it 10 wins in 11 decisions, Pelfrey will have to defeat the Yankees, a team he has beaten twice in three career tries. Pelfrey has never pitched in the new Yankee Stadium.

Taking a tip from pitching coach Dan Warthen, Dickey began exclusively throwing his harder, low-80s knuckleball -- which he was better able to command -- in the middle innings, allowing him to retire the final six batters he faced. In his most recent start, Bonderman gave up four deep flyballs to the warning track in the first two innings that were sure home runs in most ballparks. But not in spacious Comerica Park. Bonderman recovered from his shaky start and went on to allow only two runs in seven innings of work, his fifth quality start in his past six outings.

home_pitcher_note: After two successive sub-par starts, Takahashi's spot in the starting rotation seemed less than concrete going forward. His strikeout numbers aren't too impressive (61 in 93 2/3 innings) but his sinker has produced plenty of ground balls and kept hitters in the ballpark, as he's only allowed five home runs all year.

Pitching deep into contests has been an issue for Slowey this season, as he has been unable to complete six innings in 10 of his 14 starts this year. away_pitcher_note: When Pavano has been good this year, he's been very good. Pavano has also been a key at keeping the bullpen rested, pitching at least seven innings in 11 of his 14 starts this season. Next up for Pavano will be a start against the Mets. He's 7-7 with a 3.60 ERA in 20 career appearances (19 starts) vs. New York.

home_pitcher_note: Mets manager Jerry Manuel decided to leave Niese in after a one-hour rain delay in his last start against the Tigers after Niese didn't allow a single hit in his first three innings of work before the rain came. It was the first unremarkable start since coming back from the disabled list on June 5. Provided there's no rain delay, Niese will look to regain his impressive form against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a career-high 12 strikeout game against the Rockies, Baker couldn't deliver a duplicate performance against the Brewers his last time out. Baker gave up five runs on nine hits in six innings with most of the damage coming in one inning when his club held a 3-0 lead. Baker acknowledged after the start that he wasn't commanding his breaking pitches and turned to his fastball too much in a four-run inning by Milwaukee. Baker will work to mix in all of his pitches when he faces the Mets in his next start. He is 1-0 with a 3.60 ERA in one career start vs. the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco had one rough inning in his last start, but the end result worked out pretty well. After yielding two runs in a four-run second, the right-hander settled, threw seven total innings and struck out eight. He beat the Orioles and collected his first win since June 1. Nolasco faces the Mets for the fourth time. He's 1-0 with two no-decisions. On June 6 at New York, he pitched 5 1/3 innings, but the Marlins let a five-run lead slip away in a loss.
away_pitcher_note: Dickey turned in the best outing of his season in his last start, against Detroit, throwing eight shutout innings and allowing just six baserunners. He beat Florida earlier this month in Citi Field and has gone at least six innings in every 2010 start.

home_pitcher_note: The last time Robertson faced the Mets, New York scored six runs in 4 2/3 innings on June 5 at Citi Field. This time, the game will be in San Juan. It also will be Robertson's fourth start against the Mets this season. He is 2-1 against them.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers hit Takahashi with ease in his last start, as the lefty lasted only four innings before being chased after surrendering six runs. The 35-year-old rookie gave up five runs in 5 1/3 innings against the Marlins in his only start against Florida this season.

home_pitcher_note: One fastball that caught too much of the plate denied Volstad a win in his last start. Will Venable of the Padres homered, and Volstad was tagged with a hard-luck loss. For the first time this year, he didn't walk a batter. He hasn't faced New York this season.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey gave up a leadoff home run to Denard Span last time out but settled into a two-run, six-inning performance that earned him a win. He hasn't faced the Marlins yet this season but has struggled for his career against Florida, going 1-6 with 5.63 ERA in 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez is coming off one of his worst starts of the season, a 6-5 loss to the Orioles on Saturday. In that outing, Hernandez allowed five runs on 11 hits in six innings. He has faced the Mets more than any team in his career -- 34 times -- going 12-13 with a 4.38 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Santana's lack of velocity is beginning to catch up to him. For the first time since 2004, he has allowed at least four earned runs in four consecutive starts, last week giving up five in a loss to the Twins. He also gave up five in his lone start vs. the Nats this season.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Atilano earned a no-decision in a 4-3 loss to the Orioles on Sunday. He gave up three runs on five hits in seven innings.  Miguel Tejada's RBI single in the eighth was the difference. Atilano is 1-1 with a 5.59 ERA against the Mets in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off his second-worst start of the season, Niese rebounded to shut out the Twins over six innings last weekend. Relying on his cutter-curve combination, Niese struck out five and walked three. As for his worst start this year? That came against the Nats on May 11.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg will look to bounce back from the worst start of his rookie season. In the Nationals' 5-0 loss to the Braves on Monday, he allowed four runs -- three earned -- on six hits in 6 1/3 innings.  Strasburg has never faced the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: In the humidity of San Juan, Puerto Rico last Monday, Dickey suffered his first loss of the season, allowing five runs to the Marlins in five innings. His next outing comes against the Nats, against whom he allowed two runs in six innings of a no-decision on May 19.

home_pitcher_note: Stammen had his sinker working in his return from the Minors, limiting the Braves to five hits over 7 1/3 innings in a 7-2 victory on Tuesday at Atlanta. He struck out four, walked two and got 14 outs on ground balls. He also drove in a run with a sacrifice fly.
away_pitcher_note: On the day the Mets announced plans for Oliver Perez's rehab assignment, Takahashi -- he with the most tenuous grasp on a rotation spot -- served up six runs to the Marlins in 5 2/3 innings. Beating the Nationals in his first start against them could tighten his grip.

home_pitcher_note: Relying on what pitching coach Dan Warthen called horrible pitch sequences, Pelfrey gave up a career-high 12 hits in 4 2/3 innings against the Marlins on Wednesday. Though he escaped with a no-decision, he'll need to improve against a Reds team he beat last July.
away_pitcher_note: Harang pitched a strong game opposite Roy Halladay and the Phillies on Wednesday, as his only real trouble came against the bottom of the order with a Dane Sardinha three-run home run. His 5.02 ERA is the lowest it has been since his second start of the year on April 10.

home_pitcher_note: Walker has had periodic control problems, but really that's just quibbling. Overall, he's been one of the best starting pitchers in the National League and one of last offseason's best free-agent signings, with a 1.32 ERA in his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Mills recently returned from an IL stint due to a back issue. The righty has spent the bulk of this year in the bullpen, with his lone start (four innings, two runs) falling on April 13 against Milwaukee. He was 5-5 with a 4.48 ERA as a starter in 2020.

home_pitcher_note: deGrom exited his start on Friday against the Padres after only 80 pitches due to right flexor tendinitis, but the Mets expect him to be ready in time for his next one against the Cubs. They will likely monitor his workload due to the injury scare.
away_pitcher_note: Stock will make his Cubs debut on Wednesday. He was 0-3 with a 4.12 ERA in nine games for Triple-A Iowa this season, but the 31-year-old has Major League experience with 52 games for the Padres and Red Sox from 2018-'20.

home_pitcher_note: No Mets pitcher has been more consistent than Stroman, who has delivered between six and seven innings in each of his last seven starts, allowing three or fewer runs in six of them. Stroman owns a 2.49 ERA over that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks logged a quality start on Saturday, holding St. Louis to two runs over six innings. The righty struck out two, walked one and gave up three hits. He has been homer prone (19 on the season), but is 6-0 with a 2.93 ERA in his last six outings.

home_pitcher_note: Fedde has not allowed a run in his last two starts (12 innings). He is 0-2 with a 5.23 ERA in nine appearances (4 starts) against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Despite Lucchesi's recent success -- a 1.56 ERA over his last four starts -- the Mets still aren't letting him face opposing batters more than twice. Perhaps that will change after he set season highs with five innings and 72 pitches last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Ross threw eight scoreless innings with nine strikeouts in his last start on Sunday against the Giants. He earned a win vs. the Mets on April 24.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing nine runs in three innings over his first two starts of June, Peterson rebounded to deliver one of his best outings of the season, with six one-hit innings against the Cubs. He'll look to keep the momentum going in Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Lester goes for his first win of the 2021 season. Over his career, he is 7-1 with a 3.20 ERA in 10 starts against the Mets.
Corbin is riding the momentum of his best start of the season. He struck out seven and allowed one run in 8 1/3 innings on Tuesday against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Walker, who struck out a career-high 12 in his last start against the Cubs, blanked the Nationals over seven innings the first time he faced them on April 25. From that day forward, he's posted a 1.83 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: deGrom will continue his push to make ERA history after an MRI of his right shoulder showed no structural damage and he went through his between-starts routine without issue.

Stroman has completed at least six innings in eight consecutive starts, a career high. Seven of those eight have been quality starts, resulting in a 2.50 ERA over that stretch, with 46 strikeouts and 12 walks.
away_pitcher_note: Morton carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning of Thursday's win over the Cardinals. The veteran right-hander's successful outing might have been a product of him relying primarily on his fastball and curveball, which he combined to use with 87 percent of his pitches.
